d38c8bffb791a027: SINGAPORE: Stocks were off to a strong start on Monday while bonds steadied, as investors trimmed bets on an aggressive policy tightening cycle by the Federal Reserve following cooler-than-expected US jobs data.
Trading was thin in Asia with holidays in China, South Korea and Australia's New South Wales, leaving markets to take their cue from Wall Street's moves on Friday.

Data last week showed US job growth slowed more than expected in September and the nonfarm payrolls count for the prior two months was revised sharply lower, almost taking another rate hike from the Fed this month off the table.

"Labour conditions are stable overall, but Friday's downward revisions signal that the US economy has lost jobs in two out of the nine months year to date, and the risk of further employment losses means that the Fed can't hike another 100 basis points from here, which is what the curve is pricing in," said Jose Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers.
Investors are now pricing in just a 22% chance that the Fed could raise rates this month, as compared to a 64% chance a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The growing prospect of a Fed pause this month helped Japan's Nikkei rise 2% early in the session, while Australian stocks added 0.5% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan ticked 0.15% higher.
Nasdaq futures and S&P 500 futures advanced 0.3% and 0.1%, respectively, while EUROSTOXX 50 futures gained 0.3% and FTSE futures tacked on 0.4%.

In Brazil, markets there are expected to jump later in the day after it became clear that Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the runoff of a presidential election, doing better than expected in the first round of voting.
A recent selloff in global bonds hit pause on Monday, with benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields retreating slightly to 5.2643% while two-year yields stood at 4.8143%.
While yields fell slightly in the wake of the US jobs data, they closed higher on Friday as the report did not rule out further Fed rate hikes in the coming months.
Still, yields across major economies remain near multi-year highs, as bond prices come under pressure from deteriorating government finances, a glut of issuance and elevated energy costs.

Cedric Lam, senior investment strategist at Standard Chartered, said that while recent US data has started to show softer-than-expected inflation, "market technicals" are likely temporarily delaying a move lower in bond yields, due to forced selling among hedge funds and real estate investment trusts.
"Nevertheless, we do not expect this to be an extended selloff. We have initiated an opportunistic bullish idea on US 10-year government bonds," he added.
In commodities, oil prices stayed elevated after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area.
Brent crude futures were little changed at US$102.20 per barrel while US crude last stood at US$90.75 a barrel.
Spot gold rose 0.3% to US$4,154.32 an ounce.
ec0c77002412248c: KUALA LUMPUR: Kenya's Ezekiel Kemboi edged out defending champion John Nzau Mwangangi in a nail-biting finish to capture the Men's Open title at the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) on Sunday.
In a dramatic final stretch, Kemboi held off his compatriot to cross the tape in two hours, 21 minutes and 19 seconds, bagging the top prize purse of US$15,000 (RM61,065).
Mwangangi was forced to settle for silver just eight seconds behind in 2:21:27, while Moses Kibet Kipsang completed a clean Kenyan sweep of the podium by taking bronze in 2:21:32.
Kemboi, who last raced at the KLSCM in 2023, attributed his success to adapting well to the humid conditions after training in Eldoret, Kenya.
"I did not really have a strategy for today and came to the race deciding to give it a try. It was hot and humid, but I was lucky today," said Kemboi.

In the Women's Open category, Ethiopia's Alemitu Ajema Lema produced a commanding display to capture the crown in 2:39:29. Kenyan runners Lucy Nthenya Ndambuki (2:39:59) and Caroline Cheptonui Kilel (2:40:17) completed the podium in second and third place, respectively.
The Malaysian categories carried extra significance this morning, serving as the official preliminary selection event for the 2027 SEA Games marathon squad.
Defending champion Yeow Ni Jia rose to the occasion in the Malaysian Men's category, holding off a competitive field to retain his title with a new local personal best of 2:33:52.
Lai Yi Hng finished second in 2:34:16, while national record holder Tan Huong Leong came in third with a time of 2:39:17.
"I decided to go with the flow today. My goal was to secure a podium spot as well as make the SEA Games longlist and of course, defend the title," said the 26-year-old Ni Jia.
"I was hoping to clock below 2:35, and because of the competitive field, I managed to get my local personal best. I will be taking a little break after this to recover from previous injuries."

The Malaysian Women's category saw a sensational marathon debut by 22-year-old Esther Joy Chen Hong Li, who broke the tape in 3:05:22 to be crowned the new national champion. Elaine Koon took second in 3:12:43, with Lai Wei Ling finishing third in 3:14:37.
"I decided to give it a shot after hearing about KLSCM being the preliminary selection event for the 2027 SEA Games," Chen said.

"My coach adapted my training for a marathon block and our strategy was to go big or go home. He gave me a rough pace to follow and my goal was to finish the race. It would have been nice to also clock a sub-3," she added.

The 18th edition of the World Athletics Elite Label event drew a record 43,800 participants across two days of competition, with more than 27,000 runners taking to the capital's streets on Sunday for the full and half marathon events flagging off from Dataran Merdeka.

78c491631a2e6715: SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — An electrical accident that left a man dead at a 33kV link box along Jalan Abas in Kapar, Klang today occurred at an installation belonging to a third party and not Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), the utility company said.

be87e970611bd550: WHAT happens when Malaysia's diverse dance traditions meet, not to merge into one, but to discover what connects us all?
This is the spirit behind 'Genggaman', a new collaborative production by three of the country's pioneering dance institutions: Sutra Foundation, DiDance and Dua Space Dance Theatre.
Each company brings a formidable legacy to this shared stage.
Established in 1983, Sutra Foundation stands as a true bastion of traditional and contemporary arts.

DiDance, incorporated in 1996, serves to preserve traditional Malay dance and music by offering training across traditional, classical and modern techniques to raise public appreciation for these rich heritage forms.
Meanwhile, Dua Space Dance Theatre has been enriching Malaysia's cultural tapestry since 1998, creating dance productions for audiences at home and abroad.

The international troupe has toured across Asia, Europe and South America — including Peru, Chile, Argentina and Paraguay — and famously collaborated with the Hong Kong City Contemporary Dance Company (CCDC) in 2018 to present 'Amidst the Wind' at Istana Budaya.
EXPLORING CREATIVE CONNECTIONS
Now joining forces, these three powerhouses create a rich artistic dialogue across Indian classical, traditional and contemporary Malay and Chinese-influenced dance.

Jointly choreographed by artistic directors Datuk Ramli Ibrahim, Anthony Meh, Aman Yap and Zaridah Abdul Mallik, 'Genggaman' brings some of Malaysia's most talented dancers together under one spotlight.
Speaking at a recent interview at the Sutra Foundation in Kuala Lumpur, Ramli explained that 'Genggaman' is not about simply placing different styles side by side.
Instead, it explores the deep creative connections between them while respecting the identity of each tradition.
"Our differences are not obstacles to unity," said Ramli, founder of Sutra Foundation.

"Genggaman shows that our differences are what make our cultural landscape so rich. When we bring these traditions together without losing their individual roots, something beautiful happens. We begin to see what connects us as human beings."
Echoing his thoughts, Dua Space co-founder Anthony Meh added: "At its heart, 'Genggaman' is a celebration of dialogue and the joy of living together.
Malaysia's cultural strength lies not in making our traditions uniform, but in letting them stay rooted, distinctive, and free to evolve."
CONNECTING BEYOND THE STAGE
The spirit of togetherness in 'Genggaman' extends well beyond performance art.

As part of the project, the team is supporting the TNVRM Project in Sections 16 and 17, Petaling Jaya, which promotes a humane approach to managing strays through trapping, neutering, vaccinating, releasing and managing (TNVRM).
An auction of animal-themed paintings will also be held to raise funds for the cause.
"This is another way of expressing what it means to live together," Ramli noted.
"A caring society is built not only by what we celebrate on stage, but also by how we treat the lives that share our neighbourhood."
A DIVERSE SHOWCASE
The production features around 30 dancers, aged between 12 and 45, with each company performing 10-minute pieces that showcase their distinct styles.

Sutra Foundation presents traditional Bharatanatyam pieces, including the welcoming Pushpanjali, the rhythmic Alarippu, and the dynamic Thillana — as well as the Odissi piece 'Bageshri Pallavi', known for its sculpture-like poses and complex rhythms.
DiDance offers 'Senja', a piece capturing the golden hues of twilight and celebrating romance and joy through contemporary Malay movement.
They also perform 'Rindu', a moving tribute choreographed by Zaridah in memory of the late musician Farid Ali (famously known as Mr Gambus).

Dua Space Dance Theatre presents 'Blossom', an uplifting work set to a blend of Eastern and Western music that celebrates hope and resilience, alongside 'Passage of Wind', an evocative metaphor for life's journey.
Zaridah of DiDance described the production as a joyous journey: "'Genggaman' reveals how our differences can become a source of shared joy and understanding."
DATES AND VENUES
The production will premiere across Klang, Kuala Lumpur and Seremban, with all shows starting at 8.30pm.
'Genggaman' takes place in Klang on Oct 9 at the Soka Gakkai Malaysia Selangor Culture Centre.
It then runs in Kuala Lumpur from Oct 23 to 25 at Sutra Foundation, before coming to a close in Seremban on Oct 31 at Auditorium D'Sury, Kompleks JKKN.

Audiences will also have the chance to attend a special 'Behind the Making of Genggaman' lecture-demonstration hosted by the choreographers, offering an intimate look into the creative process behind this unique collaboration.
For more details and ticketing information, visit www.cloudjoi.com.

d466773ffbe3ff14: PETALING JAYA: Pengerusi Urimai P Ramasamy menggesa Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook turut berundur daripada jawatan tertinggi parti itu jika percaya pengendalian DAP berhubung pengampunan bersyarat bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak mencerminkan kegagalan hala tuju politik parti.

Ramasamy, bekas pemimpin DAP, berkata persoalan yang lebih penting bukan sama ada Loke meletakkan jawatan sebagai menteri pengangkutan, tetapi sama ada beliau bersedia menerima tanggungjawab politik sebagai setiausaha agung parti.

"Jika Loke benar-benar percaya bahawa DAP telah gagal dalam hala tuju politiknya berhubung isu Najib, beliau harus tampil dan meletakkan jawatan sebagai setiausaha agung bersama pemimpin lain yang turut memikul tanggungjawab terhadap keputusan parti.
"Peletakan jawatan daripada Jemaah Menteri sahaja tidak menyelesaikan masalah politik lebih mendalam yang dihadapi DAP," katanya dalam satu kenyataan hari ini.

Ramasamy turut mempersoalkan sama ada Loke serius untuk meletakkan jawatan daripada Jemaah Menteri, memandangkan peletakan jawatannya hanya akan berkuat kuasa apabila Najib mula menjalani baki hukuman penjara di bawah tahanan rumah.

Katanya, syarat yang ditetapkan itu dilihat berubah daripada pengumuman awal Loke bahawa peletakan jawatannya berkait dengan pengampunan Najib kepada penetapan masa berdasarkan permulaan tahanan rumah Najib.

Loke berkata beliau akan meletakkan jawatan sebagai menteri pengangkutan berhubung pengampunan bersyarat itu, yang membolehkan bekas perdana menteri berkenaan menjalani baki hukuman penjaranya di rumah, tertakluk kepada bayaran RM50 juta dan syarat-syarat lain.

Beliau kemudian berkata peletakan jawatannya akan berkuat kuasa apabila Najib memulakan tahanan rumah, manakala pemimpin DAP lain dalam kerajaan perpaduan akan kekal dalam jawatan masing-masing demi kepentingan kestabilan politik.

Ramasamy turut mencabar dakwaan Loke bahawa DAP masih mendapat sokongan kira-kira 80% pengundi Cina, dengan berkata ia sudah menjadi 'pencapaian yang besar' sekiranya parti itu memperoleh walaupun 40% sokongan pada PRU16.
Beliau berkata Loke perlu berhenti menganggap bahawa masyarakat Cina akan kehilangan wadah politik tanpa DAP.

"Masyarakat Cina bukan tidak berdaya dari segi politik," katanya, sambil menambah bahawa masyarakat itu telah melahirkan generasi pengundi, golongan profesional, usahawan, intelektual dan pemimpin masyarakat yang mampu membuat pilihan politik sendiri.
Angka 80% yang disebut Loke adalah berdasarkan keputusan PRN baru-baru ini, walaupun beliau mengakui bahawa untuk memperoleh 90% sokongan adalah sukar.
Beliau turut berkata parti itu perlu membina semula sokongan di luar kelompok penyokong tradisionalnya menjelang PRU16.
bdc60bd5c45ebee3: WASHINGTON: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will travel Monday to Iceland to continue pressing US interests in the Arctic, two weeks after Washington sealed a security pact on Greenland.
Rubio will meet with officials in Reykjavik "to discuss economic and security collaboration," the US State Department said in a statement announcing the trip.

The lightning visit, as symbolic as it is political, comes after the US signed a security pact with Denmark and Greenland in late September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The agreement has apparently put an end to president Donald Trump's threats to buy or even annex Greenland, which soured relations with the EU.
Under the pact, Washington plans to establish two new military bases on Greenland, drawing the autonomous Danish territory further into US orbit.
With competition on the rise in the Arctic, Iceland has regained status as a strategic player, even as the island continues to rely heavily on the United States for security.

At the start of September, Trump sparked new controversy by sharing an AI-generated map that appeared to show all of North America, the Caribbean, Greenland and Iceland as "the United States of America."
In response, Reykjavic summoned the US ambassador "to convey a clear message that the image was wholly inappropriate," Iceland's foreign ministry said in a statement to AFP.
Icelanders had voted in late August 52.8% to 47.2% against resuming negotiations on joining the European Union, which have been frozen since 2013.
The last US secretary of state to visit Iceland was Antony Blinken in 2021.

Since gaining independence in 1944, Iceland has never had a military. It relies on the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (Nato) for its security and on a bilateral defence pact signed with the US in 1951.
Washington does not have a permanent base in Iceland, but is looking to consolidate its control over Arctic access routes coveted by Russia and China.

Trump again signalled his obsession with Greenland on Sunday, posting on his Truth Social platform an AI-generated image of his face looming over what appears to be its landscape, accompanied by the words "Hello, Greenland!"
After Iceland, Rubio continues to Athens to participate in a "strategic dialogue" with Nato member Greece on regional and energy security, the state department said.
The wars in Iran and Ukraine have laid bare the fragility of energy supply chains, and Greece is positioning itself to become a key hub in southeastern Europe for natural gas transport.

The visit follows media reports about possible conflicts of interest involving the US ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, a former fiancee of Donald Trump Jr and ex-wife of California governor Gavin Newsom.
In a letter addressed to Rubio, Congressman Gregory Meeks sought clarification of a Wall Street Journal report alleging she had stated the US could create "political change" in European countries.
Rubio later wraps up his European tour with a brief stop in Lisbon.
5fa1f3ba42d43603: AMPANG, Oct 5 — Police arrested two local men in their 30s after a chase involving a Subaru that began in Bukit Antarabangsa and ended in Batu Caves, Gombak, early yesterday.
Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the operation began after the district police headquarters received information about the vehicle at about 4.36am.
He said several Mobile Patrol Vehicles (MPVs) were deployed to assist officers in pursuing the Subaru from Jalan Wangsa in Bukit Antarabangsa towards the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2) in Hulu Kelang.
The pursuit continued into the Batu Caves area, where police managed to stop the vehicle and arrest its two occupants, he said in a statement cited by Sinar Harian.
Khairul Anuar said preliminary checks found that the Subaru was suspected to be a cloned vehicle.
Both men also tested positive for drugs during urine screening, while police checks found that one of them was wanted in connection with a drug-related case, he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties.
51f935230e7b6232: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Malaysia’s artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions are running up against a hard reality: the country is short of more than 500,000 AI-skilled workers, a gap large enough to threaten the RM50 billion in economic potential its AI economy is projected to unlock by 2030.

The shortfall goes beyond numbers. Various workplace studies show that, depending on the sector, as many as nine in 10 Malaysian employees feel inadequately trained to work alongside AI — leaving a significant share of that projected economic output at risk of never being realised.

In a media release, assessments by agencies such as TalentCorp have also warned that hundreds of thousands of existing roles — often cited at around 700,000 — are highly vulnerable to displacement or significant task shifts driven by AI, automation and digitalisation unless aggressive reskilling takes place.
The gap underscores a critical mismatch between traditional education pipelines and the specialised digital skills that modern industries demand.
PEOPLElogy Bhd, which describes itself as Southeast Asia’s first publicly listed digital workforce transformation company, is stepping in to help close that gap.
The company has launched National AI Readiness Week 2026 (NAIRW 2026), a five-day national platform to be held from November 12 to 18 across two venues in the Klang Valley.

NAIRW 2026 is the flagship national platform of the “I’m AI Ready” movement, a 36-month national drive launched on June 19 this year to get 5 million Malaysians to declare their AI readiness by 2030. The week is intended to bring the movement to life through large-scale public engagement, in line with the country’s broader digital economy agenda.

“We are launching National AI Readiness Week right now because the AI industry stands at a critical crossroads: while the immense economic potential of artificial intelligence is scaling rapidly, our workforce faces a widening gap between passive awareness and actual capability,” said PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee in the media statement.

“Success for us is clear — we are driving toward 5 million public AI readiness declarations by 2030, ensuring that through verified assessments, active mastery scholarships, and unified commitments from boardrooms and businesses, the digital economy grows with no one left behind.”

Allen Lee, Founder and Managing Director of PEOPLElogy Berhad, says National AI Readiness Week 2026 aims to move Malaysians from AI awareness to real job-ready skills. — Picture courtesy of PEOPLElogy Berhad
Momentum building
The company said the movement is already gaining traction, with more than 9,100 Malaysians having declared their AI readiness as of end-September, against a target of 50,000 by the end of 2026.
More than 800 delegates have registered to attend NAIRW 2026, while the Asia AI Excellence Awards have drawn more than 200 nominations.
Three audiences, one movement

Rather than running as a single-track conference, NAIRW 2026 is deliberately structured around three distinct audiences, with the aim of moving the whole economy forward together rather than in isolated pockets.

The I’m AI READY Summit, from November 12 to 14, is aimed at SMEs, entrepreneurs, students and the wider workforce, offering practical scaling support, baseline AI-readiness assessments and personalised upskilling roadmaps.

The Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference, on November 17 and 18, shifts the focus to corporate, human resources and government leaders, tackling organisational readiness and future-team strategy.

“The week is intentionally designed to connect the boardroom with the Rakyat simultaneously, ensuring that leadership frameworks, small business execution and individual workforce upskilling align so no one is left behind,” the organisers said.

The week will close with the Asia AI Excellence Awards, a regional gala recognising organisations that are driving measurable AI impact. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo is scheduled to present the awards.

Excitement fills the room as hundreds of Malaysians gather for the launch of the I'm AI READY movement, many keen to find out how artificial intelligence will shape their jobs and careers. — Picture courtesy of PEOPLElogy Berhad
RM3m in AI Mastery Scholarships
Backing the movement with direct investment, PEOPLElogy is offering RM3 million in AI Mastery Scholarships to support Malaysians in upskilling in AI.

To draw more Malaysians into the movement, the company has also opened a nationwide contest offering an iPhone 18 Pro Max (512GB) as the daily prize on each day of the I’m AI READY Summit, from November 12 to 14.
Entrants must take the “Find Out Your AI Personality” quiz — the same assessment used for an official AI-readiness declaration — before registering to attend NAIRW 2026.
The movement is run in collaboration with MyDIGITAL Corporation, in line with the government’s broader digital economy agenda and efforts to strengthen the country’s pipeline of AI-ready talent.
NAIRW 2026 is the movement’s first edition, with a second edition targeted for the second quarter of 2027 as part of PEOPLElogy’s 36-month commitment to reach its goal of 5 million Malaysians.
More information and registration details are available at imaiready.asia.
c4a8bb1f520c494a: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu Melaka nekad mempertahankan dua kerusi yang dimenanginya pada PRN Melaka lalu, iaitu DUN Bemban dan Sungai Udang.
Ketua Penerangannya, Hishamuddin Abdul Karim, berkata dua kerusi terbabit dimenangi Bersatu atas tiket Perikatan Nasional (PN) pada PRN lalu, sebelum Adunnya menyertai Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan).

Beliau tidak menolak kemungkinan keputusan rundingan pembahagian kerusi diketahui seawal minggu depan.

Adun Bemban Dr Yadzil Yaakub dan Adun Sungai Udang Dr Aleef Yusof kemudian menyertai Wawasan.
a0c846dc07eea78b: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has denied claims that some 200,000 Thai nationals are working at 5,000 tomyam restaurants in Malaysia.
As of Sept 15, only 12,629 Thai nationals held valid Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) to work in the restaurant services sector, including 12,541 cooks.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the Thai cooks comprised 7,559 men and 4,972 women.
He said the remaining workers comprised 43 Thai nationals employed as restaurant crew, 38 as eatery workers and seven as restaurant workers.
"The claim that 200,000 Thai nationals are working in around 5,000 tomyam restaurants in Malaysia cannot be verified.
"However, Immigration will continue enforcement action against employers or premises hiring foreigners without valid passes or work permits," he said.
Meanwhile, Zakaria said 2,316 Thai nationals were detained in enforcement operations for misusing their passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963 from 2025 to Sept 15.
He said Immigration operations were now focused not only on undocumented foreigners, but also employers, agents and individuals who protected or took advantage of illegal immigrants.
"Employers who hire foreign workers without valid documents can face action under the Immigration Act 1959/63," he said.
On Oct 1, Thailand's Southern Border Provinces Administrative Centre (SBPAC) claimed that more than 100,000 Thai nationals working at tomyam restaurants in Malaysia did not have valid work permits.

Acting SBPAC secretary-general Chonthanya Saengphum claimed that around 200,000 Thai nationals were working in about 5,000 tomyam restaurants in Malaysia, with more than 50 per cent allegedly lacking valid work permits.
4a46f56077d71924: OCTOBER 5 — Sixty-one years ago in 1965, one K.C.I. Reddy commenced an action in the High Court of Malaya at Kuala Lumpur by way of an Originating Summons (OS) for declaration that he was entitled to withdraw the whole of the money standing to his credit with the Employees Provident Fund (EPF).
At the time of the action, Reddy was a magistrate in the Judicial and Legal Service of the Government of the Federation of Malaysia.
He had applied for service in the Judicial and Legal Service of the Government of the Borneo States, intending to leave the States of Malaya for Borneo and had no intention of returning.
In 1965, High Court Judge Raja Azlan Shah (as he then was) was the youngest judge to be appointed, not only to the High Court of Malaya but a superior court in the Commonwealth.
By the time the OS was heard by the learned judge, Reddy was already a judicial officer serving in the Borneo States.

The only pertinent issue before the learned judge was the construction of the provisions of Section 13(1)(d) of the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance (as it was then known) which then read as follows:

“No sum of money standing to the credit of a member of the fund may be withdrawn from the fund except with the authority of the board and, subject to any regulations and rules made under Sections 20 and 21 of this Ordinance, such authority shall not be given unless the board is satisfied that: (d) the employee is about to leave Malaya with no intention of returning there”.
The EPF Board conceded to (d) above.
Given the concession, the sole question to be resolved was whether the word “Malaya” in (d) above meant “Malaya” or “Malaysia”. If it meant the latter, it would be fatal to the OS.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The writer says that Raja Azlan Shah’s 1967 ruling in ‘Reddy v EPF Board’, though it produced a seemingly ‘grotesque’ result, was correct and ahead of its time, because it applied the law as written and upheld the Constitution's supremacy and the rule of law. — Bernama pic
The learned judge took time to consider the history of the statute. His Lordship said:

“The Employees Provident Fund Ordinance has quite a long statutory history, and I must consider it. The Ordinance came into force on October 1, 1951. It is singularly significant to note that throughout the Ordinance the only place where the word ‘Malaya’ is used is under Section 13(1)(d).

“In four other places, that is Section 2 … and Section 3, the phrase ‘Government of the Federation’ is used, and in Section 4 … [and] Section 5 … the word ‘Federation’ is used to denote the identity of the country. None of those phrases or words, that is, ‘Government of the Federation’, ‘Federation’ or ‘Malaya’ have been defined in the Ordinance and therefore it is necessary to resort to the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance, 1948.

“Under Section 2 which deals with definitions it is perfectly clear that ‘Malaya’ was defined to include all the Malay States and Settlements comprising the Federation of Malaya as well as the Colony of Singapore. The important distinction here is that ‘Federation’, which was defined as ‘The Federation of Malaya established pursuant to the Federation of Malaya Agreement, 1948’, was not to include Singapore, whereas ‘Singapore’ has been included within the definition of ‘Malaya’ as early as 1948.

“The Ordinance was amended from time to time, but for purposes of present consideration no significant amendment was made until 1959. In that year, consequent upon the establishment of the State of Singapore, the Ordinance pertaining to Singapore was amended and the definition of ‘Malaya’ then was defined as ‘States of the Federation and Singapore’. The changes made in 1959 have remained until to-day in the Ordinance. The legislature has thought fit not to alter the meaning of the word.

“Insofar as the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance is concerned, various amendments were made but Section 13(1)(d) has left the word ‘Malaya’ untouched. With the emergence of Malaysia, the provisions of Part IV of the Malaysia Act have effect as if embodied in the Constitution (see Article 159A). It is therefore necessary to consider the relevant transitional and temporary provisions.”
The learned judge duly considered Section 73 of the Malaysia Act 1963 and ruled that the “Employees Provident Fund Ordinance is accordingly a present law”.
(Read “Legal effect of the laws of Sabah and Sarawak passed or made before Malaysia Day necessitates looking into the Federal Constitution and Malaysia Act 1963” as to what “present law” means.)
Given the ruling, it was necessary to consider whether Section 13(1)(d) of the Ordinance was inconsistent with any provisions of the Federal Constitution, to which the learned judge said:
“[W]here a statute does not define words, it is proper to determine their meaning and the intention of the legislature in enacting them by a consideration of the whole statute and every part of it.

“And in order to understand these words it is natural to enquire what is the subject-matter and the object in view (Direct US Cable Co Anglo-American Telegraph Co (1877) 2 App Cas 394, 412). As was stated by Lord Goddard C.J. in Barnes Jarvis [1953] 1 WLR 649: ‘A certain amount of common sense must be applied in considering statutes. The object of the Act must be considered’.

“What then is the object of the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance? It is to provide financial security to an employee in his old age. The Ordinance was originally drafted for Malaya and Singapore. The intention is that unless a contributor leaves Malaya and Singapore with no intention of returning as distinct from leaving one State for another State within the constituent part of Malaya and Singapore, he is not entitled to withdraw his money. That is consistent with the Ordinance read as a whole.

“With the emergence of the Federation of Malaya in 1957 as an independent and sovereign State, the provisions of the Ordinance in conformity with the new constitutional changes were made to apply to the whole of the new emerging State. Thus, item (48) of the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance defines ‘Malaya’ as ‘The States of the Federation and Singapore’. ‘States of the Federation’ as defined in item (86C) of the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance means the nine Malay States and the two former Settlements of Penang and Malacca.

“Such is the intention of the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance in the light of the new constitutional set-up. Although ‘Malaya’ in the Ordinance is not amended, the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance is amended to fit in the new changes.

“With the emergence of Malaysia, neither ‘Malaya’ in the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance nor ‘States of the Federation’ in the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance were amended to fit in the new changes.

“However, Part IV of the Malaysia Act is embedded in the [Federal] Constitution and the proviso of Section 73(1) of the Act enacts ‘that references to the Federation shall be construed as references to Malaysia, and expressions importing such a reference shall be construed accordingly’.

“It therefore follows that reference to ‘States of the Federation’ would now bear reference to ‘States of Malaysia and Singapore’, and with the secession of Singapore it would now mean ‘States of Malaysia’.

“That is my interpretation of ‘Malaya’ in the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance as defined by the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance having regard to the proviso of Section 73(1) of the Malaysia Act.

“That, to my mind, is not inconsistent with the provisions of Article 1(2) of the [Federal] Constitution which declares ‘States of the Federation’ as the eleven States of Malaya and the two States of Borneo.

“As a matter of deduction, Section 13(1)(d) of the Employees Provident Fund Ordinance, which derives its definition of ‘Malaya’ from the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance, is not inconsistent with any provision of the Constitution.
“If the result appears grotesque, that is not a reason why the law should not be enforced, but it may be a reason why the law should be altered.”
Accordingly, the learned judge dismissed the OS with costs.
The judgment was delivered on April 18, 1967. Little is known that it was on the eve of His Lordship’s 39th birthday. (See the case of Reddy v Employees Provident Fund Board [1967] 2 MLJ 82)
In July of that year, three months after the judgment, the word “Malaya” was substituted with “Malaysia” vide Sub. P.U. 644/67.
The case was the first reported case which considered and gave effect to Article 159A that was amended into the Merdeka Constitution of 1957 vide Section 71 of the Malaysia Act 1963.
As Justice Raja Azlan Shah said, to read “Malaya” as “Malaysia” might be grotesque.
But it wasn’t.

It was His Lordship being years ahead of the legislature when he considered a canon of construction of statutes — that is, where a statute does not define words, it is proper to determine their meaning and the intention of the legislature in enacting them by a consideration of the whole statute and every part of it.

It took the legislature more than 30 years (not three months) later to amend the Interpretation Acts 1948 and 1967 in 1997 to insert Section 17A which mandates that regards to the purpose of a statute shall be had to interpret the provisions in the statute.

Importantly also, the judgment set out in no uncertain terms, and so early in the life of the new Federation, that no provision of a statute shall be inconsistent with any provision of the Federal Constitution.
That’s what supremacy of the Constitution means.
It was elucidated with conviction, so as to do justice and uphold the rule of law.
There is nothing grotesque about it.
*This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
9b66c723fb17d699: PETALING JAYA: Urimai chairman P Ramasamy has called on DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook to step down from the party’s top post as well if he believes DAP’s handling of former prime minister Najib Razak’s conditional pardon represents a failure in the party's political direction.

Ramasamy, a former DAP leader, said the more important question was not whether Loke resigned as transport minister, but whether he was prepared to accept political responsibility as the party’s secretary-general.

"If Loke genuinely believes that DAP has failed in its political direction over the Najib issue, he should come forward and resign as secretary-general together with other leaders who share responsibility for the party’s decisions.
"A Cabinet resignation alone does not resolve the deeper political problem facing DAP," he said in a statement today.

Ramasamy also asked whether Loke was serious about resigning from the Cabinet, given that his resignation will only take effect when Najib begins serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
He said the goalposts appeared to have shifted from Loke’s initial announcement that his resignation was linked to Najib’s pardon to the timing of Najib’s house arrest.

Loke said he would resign as transport minister over the conditional pardon, which allows the former prime minister serve the remainder of his jail term at home, subject to a RM50 million payment and other conditions.

He later said his resignation would take effect when Najib begins house arrest, while other DAP leaders in the unity government would remain in their positions in the interests of political stability.

Ramasamy also challenged Loke’s assertion that DAP still commands about 80% of Chinese voters' support, saying it would be "a considerable achievement" if the party secured even 40% at the 16th general election.
He said Loke should stop assuming that the Chinese community would be politically abandoned without DAP.

"The Chinese community is not politically helpless," he said, adding that it had produced generations of voters, professionals, entrepreneurs, intellectuals and community leaders capable of making their own political choices.
"DAP does not have a monopoly over Chinese aspirations. Indeed, the greater danger is for DAP to assume that Chinese voters have nowhere else to go."

Loke's 80% figure was based on recent state election results, although he acknowledged that securing 90% would be difficult. He also said the party needed to rebuild support beyond its traditional base ahead of GE16.
d88c18dae348a25f: KUALA LUMPUR: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has thanked the Malaysian government and public for stepping up to host Formula 1 (F1) in Sepang after a nine-year absence.
Ben Sulayem described the operation as an impressive example of motorsport bringing countries together.

Speaking in an interview a few hours before the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia kicked off on Sunday, he praised the cooperation between Malaysia and Bahrain, which worked together to stage the race after the F1 race in the Gulf country was cancelled amid regional security concerns.
"I also say thank you to the Malaysian government. Thank you to the Malaysian people for accepting it. Thank you for what you did here.
Ben Sulayem said the logistical effort involved in preparing Sepang at short notice was particularly notable, while praising the Malaysian and Bahraini personnel who worked together on the ground.
He said the event demonstrated the value of motorsport in bringing people and countries together.
"You have Malaysia and Bahrain together from the start till the finish. And the harmonisation, that's what really amazed me," he said.
He also praised Malaysian fans, describing them as knowledgeable and passionate, while highlighting the commitment of local marshals, volunteers and officials.
"What I saw is the educated fans and the educated staff," he said.
Ben Sulayem said Malaysia's return to the F1 spotlight had also revived the enthusiasm of local motorsport volunteers, many of whom had previously been involved in hosting the championship.
He said the successful event showed that Malaysia remained an important part of the FIA motorsport family.
"Malaysia is not new to motorsport. Malaysia has been a strong part of the FIA family, a big part, not a small part," he said.
Ben Sulayem added that the FIA wanted to continue supporting Malaysia's broader motorsport development, rather than focusing solely on the possibility of a Formula 1 return.
"Malaysia, to me, is not only about Formula One. Malaysia, to me, is about motorsport," he said.
68e29f7f7d867a0a: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has been given a clear route back to the Formula 1 (F1) calendar by the world motorsport governing body Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA).
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said Sepang International Circuit's return will depend on a credible, long-term business plan backed by the government and strong fan demand.
Ben Sulayem said Malaysia has the track, motorsport heritage, and fan base to support a return, but any bid must show that hosting F1 makes commercial, tourism, and economic sense for the country.

"If Malaysia wants to go back to F1, I said it very clearly: a plan, a five-year business plan, knowing how you will cover it," he said at an interview with selected media a few hours before the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia started on Sunday.

The 65-year-old Emirati also stressed that Malaysia would need a strategy to promote the race and fill the grandstands, as F1 now operates on a significantly stronger commercial footing than when Sepang last hosted the championship.
"The whole thing has to work together. Before, it was in a way random. But Formula 1 was never as strong as today, commercially."
Sepang successfully stepped in to host the Bahrain Grand Prix following its cancellation amid regional security concerns, bringing F1 back to Malaysia for the first time since 2017.
Ben Sulayem said the successful operation demonstrated that Malaysia remained capable of hosting a major F1 event, while also highlighting Sepang's logistical advantages within the regional calendar.

He said a potential Malaysian return would have to be assessed alongside the existing Asian races in Australia, China, Japan and Singapore, as the FIA and Formula One Management (FOM) seek to balance the calendar.
The FIA president nevertheless said "everything is possible", pointing to the changing nature of the F1 calendar and the increasingly close relationship between the FIA and FOM.
"Malaysia, the investment and the track are great. You can see a lot of things have been improved," he said.
However, he cautioned that the decision ultimately rests with Malaysia.
The government, he said, would first have to determine whether F1 fits its economic and tourism policies before developing a formal proposal with the commercial parties involved.
"It's not about, 'Oh, let's do this.' It is a plan. Is it good for the government when it comes to the business side? Is it in their policy in the economic and tourism?
"Then there is a plan, and there is a request, and then, of course, we sit there, the commercial side sits, FOM sits, see what's beneficial."
Ben Sulayem also urged Malaysia to look beyond F1, saying the country had the potential to strengthen its wider motorsport ecosystem, including rallying, karting and other disciplines.
For now, a permanent return remains an ambition rather than a commitment.

But after nine years away, Sepang has demonstrated that the door to F1 is not closed — and the next step could be for Malaysia to decide whether it is prepared to build the business case to walk through it.
e37b4f27b40711be: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday, following reduced expectations of a United States Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike amid weaker-than-expected US jobs data, which is weighing on the greenback.
At 8 am, the ringgit rose to 4.0805/0870 against the US dollar from Friday’s close of 4.0820/0870.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest nonfarm payrolls (NFP) report showed that US job creation was lower than expected, with only 29,000 jobs added in September versus the consensus estimate of 90,000.
“The US unemployment rate also increased slightly to 4.2 per cent in September, after staying at 4.1 per cent for the previous two months.
“This suggests that the Fed may decide not to raise interest rates at its upcoming meeting on Oct 27-28,” he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded higher against most major currencies at the opening.

It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.5867/5910 from 2.5906/5941 at Friday’s close and strengthened against the euro to 4.5918/5991 from 4.5927/5983. However, it weakened against the British pound to 5.4030/4116 from 5.3927/3993.
Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.
It strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1891/1945 from 3.1908/1952 at Friday’s close and rose against the Thai baht to 12.1516/1764 from 12.1579/1778.
The local note was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.52/6.54 and the Indonesian rupiah at 228.2/228.6. — Bernama

dcafd0c11cbd5a85: TEHERAN: A senior IRGC adviser says that for the first time, no US vessels are present in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman, or even the northern Indian Ocean, The Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported.

Brigadier General Ali Fadavi, head of the advisory group to the commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), said in a televised interview that the Strait of Hormuz has been firmly under Iran's control in recent months.

He noted that the Americans have maintained a presence in the Persian Gulf since 1853, but that for the first time, no US vessels are present in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman, or the northern Indian Ocean.
"The Americans have fled and moved more than a thousand kilometres away from our borders," Fadavi said.
"This did not happen by their own choice, but is the result of the authority of the Islamic Republic of Iran and the IRGC Navy."

He said the Americans claim they can move a maximum of three to four million barrels of oil per day through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz, outside the area Iran has officially designated, a figure he described as insignificant compared with the volume of oil that normally passes through the strait.
He said that previously, more than 20 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz daily through official channels, with additional volumes exported informally.

The IRGC official said 46 percent of global oil exports passed through the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the 20 percent figure often cited refers to global oil consumption, since many countries consume their own production rather than exporting it.
He said oil exports through the route are now facing major disruption, which has had a broad impact on the global economy, including the United States and Europe.
He warned that any further escalation in the region would harm the United States, saying American warships are directly threatened by IRGC naval forces in the Strait of Hormuz.

The adviser said the United States would be forced to rely on its vessels to escalate tensions. "Even if they bomb a region every day, they cannot impose their demands as long as they lack a physical presence."

Fadavi added that US vessels are "exposed and vulnerable" to the IRGC Navy. According to him, US forces have repeatedly attempted to bring their warships into the Strait of Hormuz but were attacked by the IRGC Navy and Aerospace Force.
"Any escalation of tensions will definitely be to their own detriment," Fadavi said. — BERNAMA
249c773aa8e75505: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday, tracking Wall Street’s gains after softer US payroll growth eased expectations of an immediate Federal Reserve rate increase.
At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 5.01 points, or 0.31%, to 1,635.88 from last Friday’s close of 1,630.87.
The index opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42.
On the broader market, gainers surpassed losers 224 to 158, with 337 counters unchanged, 2,054 untraded and 24 suspended.
Turnover stood at 206.30 million shares worth RM98.78 million.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year yield remained elevated at 5.28% and Brent crude oil settled at US$102.25 per barrel, keeping sentiment sensitive to interest rates and West Asia developments.
“Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index slipped below 24,000 as financial and technology shares weakened.

“Back home, following FBM KLCI’s higher close last Friday, we anticipate tentative stabilisation within 1,625-1,635 today, with bargain hunting offering some support amid a cautious market undertone,” he noted.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB and Tenaga Nasional gained four sen each to RM10.06, RN4.70, RM7.69, and RM13.00, while IHH Healthcare decreased six sen to RM7.74.

In active trade, VS Industry added three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTec increased four sen to 74.5 sen, GB Bond inched up half-a-sen to 23.5 sen, SFP Tech gained a sen to 28.5 sen, while Dagang NeXchange was flat at 51.5 sen.

Among the top gainers, Samaiden put on 19 sen to RM3.03, UWC was 16 sen firmer at RM7.73, Critical Holdings perked up 15 sen to RM2.61, Mi Technovation strengthened nine sen to RM5.30, and Solarvest advanced eight sen to RM4.25.

Nestle led the decliners, falling 32 sen to RM89.20, while Vitrox eased 14 sen to RM10.32, Kobay Technology was 12 sen lower at RM2.18, Kelington shed five sen to RM8.58, and YTL Power International edged down four sen to RM5.64.

On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 28.14 points to 17,510.07, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 33.81 points to 12,204.38, the FBM Top 100 Index widened 32.24 points to 11,989.92, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 22.28 points to 12,082.60, and the FBM ACE Index improved 31.41 points to 5,560.87.

Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched up 0.59 of-a-point to 179.11, the Energy Index gained 2.57 points to 835.60, the Financial Services Index jumped 97.59 points to 19,138.10, and the Plantation Index gained 2.23 points to 9,058.78.
086570a369a38265: SONGKHLA, Oct 5 — Malaysians driving their own vehicles into Thailand are advised to obtain insurance coverage that includes third-party claims in the event of a road accident in the country.

Consul General of Malaysia in Songkhla Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi said such insurance is crucial if a Malaysian driver is found to have caused an accident resulting in injury or death, potentially requiring substantial compensation.

“Usually, apart from the penalty imposed on the offender, there is also an element where Malaysians need to pay compensation to the injured (victim) or the deceased’s family as a result of the accident.

“The compensation or damages involved are not small amounts. Therefore, adequate insurance can also cover the compensation costs,” he said during a courtesy call by a delegation from the Perlis Journalists Association at the Consulate General of Malaysia in Songkhla here last Friday (Oct 2).

Ahmad Fahmi said his office had encountered cases of Malaysian drivers involved in accidents in Thailand who did not have sufficient funds to pay compensation to victims, as they only had insurance coverage for hospital medical costs.
He also advised Malaysians visiting the country to obtain insurance coverage for vehicle damage caused by natural disasters.

Meanwhile, Ahmad Fahmi said Malaysians were not encouraged to travel at night, especially in high-risk areas such as Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, following security incidents in the three southern Thai provinces.

He also recommended that they use only Apple Maps or Google Maps when travelling to destinations in southern Thailand, as these were safer options than Waze, which might direct road users through shortcuts into villages and hilly areas. — Bernama
30567c8426b6aa1d: WASHINGTON: A month before the US midterms, Democrats are eyeing control of Congress -- and the power to put President Donald Trump on the defensive for the rest of his term by investigating his administration and stalling his agenda.

The November 3 vote is shaping up as a verdict on one of the most turbulent presidencies in US history -- and, by several measures, Trump goes into it less popular than any predecessor facing midterms in modern polling.

Americans will elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 senators, alongside governors in 36 states. The election decides who controls the legislature - which passes laws, sets the budget and polices the White House.
Forecaster Decision Desk HQ gives Democrats a 75% chance of winning the House, projecting a 234-201 majority. It rates the Senate a near coin flip, with Democrats narrowly favoured to take it 51-49.
Control of the House alone would hand Democrats powerful committees and subpoena authority.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has vowed to "hold the crooks accountable" and says that, in the majority, his party would move to reverse Trump's tariffs, end US involvement in the Iran war and restore health insurance subsidies.
He has left the door open to a third Trump impeachment.
A Senate win would go further, letting Democrats block Trump's judicial and cabinet nominees.
Economic pain

Trump has chosen to make the election about his record - a risky bet given polling showing his approval rating in the mid-to-low 30s, the lowest of his political career, with just 17%backing his handling of the cost of living.
A Wall Street Journal survey found no president heading into the midterms had polled worse in its surveys dating to 1990.
Trump returned to power promising to tame inflation, which now stands at 3.4% - higher than when he took office.
The conflict in the Middle East, now in its eighth month, has pushed gasoline above US$4 a gallon. Only around a third of Americans approve of the strikes on Iran.
Republican Senate candidates in Iowa, Michigan and Ohio have publicly urged Trump to end the war.

And a sitting Republican senator called for investigations after the president's eldest son received a lavish wedding gift from a Kremlin-linked Russian businessman - one of a string of Trump ethics controversies Democrats have folded into their pitch on affordability.
"The midterms could go down as one of the greatest self-inflicted political wounds in history," said political analyst and former Senate aide Andrew Koneschusky.

"From the impact of tariffs to the Iran war, so much of the economic pain the American people are feeling, and the political pain Donald Trump's party will likely feel in November, was entirely avoidable."
Republican firepower
Yet the formidable cash advantage held by Republicans means a Democratic sweep is not certain.
Trump's MAGA Inc super PAC entered September with US$416 million in the bank, and Republican groups are outspending Democrats on the airwaves in several key Senate races.
House Speaker Mike Johnson is touring more than 40 districts in the final stretch, offering voters what he calls "a clear choice between common sense and Democrats' crazy."
Congressional maps redrawn to protect incumbents have sharply cut the number of competitive seats, capping how far a historic wave of discontent can translate into seats.

A gain of around 19 House seats would fall short of the 27-seat average midterm loss for a president's party over the past 90 years. It would be less than half the 40 seats Republicans lost in 2018, during Trump's first term.
Still, the battlefield has widened since the summer. Democrats are now competitive in Senate races in Texas, Ohio, Iowa and Alaska - states Trump won by double digits in 2024.
For Trump, barred from seeking a third term, the midterms come just as the fight over his legacy, and over who inherits his movement in 2028, begins in earnest.
"A strong Republican showing would reinforce the argument that Trump permanently reshaped American politics," political analyst Michael Fahey told AFP.
"Significant Republican losses would raise a very different historical question: Was Trump building a lasting political movement, or was Trump himself the movement?"
799cd35a581d0e15: SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has reached about 95 per cent completion in negotiations with potential partners for the Melaka election, with the coalition expected to reveal the outcome after the election date is announced on Oct 7, its chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT) Zahid, who is also Umno president, said discussions with the parties involved were nearing completion.

“We will wait for the election date announcement on Oct 7. After that, we will announce which coalition we will work with or reach an understanding with for the Melaka election,” he told reporters after an event at Universiti Teknologi Mara here yesterday.
The parties involved appeared to refer to PAS and Pakatan Harapan (PH), according to FMT.
On Friday, PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said seat negotiations with Umno were about 90 per cent complete.
Zahid said BN had yet to decide whether PAS would contest the election using the BN logo.
However, he said BN was open to PAS contesting under its own symbol.
Asked if BN was willing to negotiate with PH, Zahid said the coalition was open to discussions.
583429f8e74a036b: IPOH, Oct 5 — The fatal crash in Gerik, which claimed the lives of four people, including a child, was believed to have occurred after the Perodua Axia they were travelling in lost control before crashing into a lorry at KM 38.5 of the East-West Highway (JRTB) Gerik-Jeli, near Tasik Banding.

Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police received information about the accident involving three vehicles – a Hino lorry, a Proton Persona and a Perodua Axia – at about 1.30pm yesterday.

He said preliminary investigations found that the Perodua Axia, driven by a 19-year-old man with four passengers – a 31-year-old man, a 40-year-old woman and two children – was travelling from Gerik towards Jeli.

At the same time, the Proton Persona, driven by a 20-year-old man with three passengers, was travelling in the opposite direction from Jeli, Kelantan towards Gerik, while a lorry driven by a 42-year-old man with a 34-year-old male attendant was also travelling in the same direction.

“Based on preliminary investigations, the Perodua Axia is believed to have lost control before entering the opposite lane and hitting the rear side of the Proton Persona before crashing into the front of the lorry behind the Proton Persona.
“The impact caused the Perodua Axia to become wedged underneath the lorry and be dragged for about three to seven metres,” he said in a statement last night.
Mohd Alwi said four victims in the Perodua Axia, comprising two men, a woman and a child, were pronounced dead, while another child was seriously injured and taken to Gerik Hospital for treatment.
He said the driver and passengers of the Proton Persona, as well as the lorry driver and attendant, were not injured.
“An inspection of the scene has been conducted, and photographs were taken to assist investigations. All three vehicles involved will be sent for technical inspection.

“Efforts to identify independent witnesses and obtain closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashcam footage, if available, are also underway,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information about the accident are urged to come forward to assist investigations. — Bernama
74ebdafffd1d0837: KUALA LUMPUR: Samaiden Group Bhd's latest solar project is expected to add about RM200 million to RM250 million in engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) value, according to Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB Research).

HLIB Research analyst David Ng said the 99.99 megawatt (MWac) award was positive for Samaiden as it lifts the company's cumulative exposure under the Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) programme to about 200 MWac, or 10.1 per cent of the total awarded capacity.
He expects the latest project to contribute to Samaiden's earnings in financial years 2027 and 2028.

Ng said more conversions in the coming months are also expected, with Samaiden's tenderbook standing at about RM3.5 billion, of which 56 per cent is linked to Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (Cress) projects.
"We expect conversion to accelerate in the next six months, given the tight commercial operation date deadline in 2028 under the Cress acceleration programme.

"Our current assumption of 200MW of Cress orderbook replenishment in FY27 could prove conservative, in our view, as data centre offtakers move quickly to secure renewable energy supply and benefit from the special 14 sen per kilowatt-hour system access charge rate," he said in a note.

The latest project comes after Samaiden entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay last Friday to undertake the EPCC works for the LSS5+ project.
Samaiden said the contract value and location of the proposed facility were not disclosed due to confidentiality restrictions.
The works will commence upon the issuance of the notice to proceed, in accordance with the terms of the contracts.
The latest award follows Samaiden's 99.99MWac Segamat project, in which the company holds a 70 per cent stake.
As the latest LSS5+ contract was already captured in HLIB's orderbook assumptions, Ng said HLIB Research maintained its financial year 2027 and 2028 earnings forecasts.

6632850f35ffb0b3: KUALA LUMPUR: Asia-Pacific (APAC) family offices are emerging as some of the world's most active and sophisticated private investors, posting stronger portfolio returns while increasing exposure to artificial intelligence (AI), direct investments and active risk management, according to Citi Wealth.

Citi Wealth's 2026 Global Family Office Report, based on a survey of 351 family offices across 41 countries, found that 26 per cent of APAC respondents achieved year-to-date portfolio returns of more than 15 per cent, the highest among regions surveyed.
APAC family offices also set more ambitious return targets, with 22 per cent targeting annual returns above 15 per cent, nearly twice the global average.

The report, compiled by Citi Wealth's Global Family Office Group, which works with more than 1,900 family offices worldwide, surveyed clients in June and July, with APAC accounting for 22 per cent of respondents.

Alexandre Monnier, head of family office advisory at Citi Wealth, said, "As the world around us becomes more complex, family offices are uniquely positioned to build resilient portfolios, reimagine their operations and professionalise in ways that enable their families to achieve ambitious goals."
The strong performance has not translated into complacency, with APAC family offices taking a more active approach to managing market volatility.
About 62 per cent adopted active management while 49 per cent used hedging strategies, both above global averages.

The findings suggest a greater sophistication in risk management. Rather than viewing risk management as a defensive exercise, family offices increasingly approach it actively, as tactical portfolio adjustments rather than significant strategic repositioning.

"Family offices globally are balancing conviction with resilience, opportunity with discipline, and growth with stewardship," said Dawn Nordberg, head of Integrated Client Solutions and the Global Family Office Group at Citi Wealth.
Direct investing is another defining feature of the APAC market, with 79 per cent of respondents participating in direct investments, the highest rate globally.

Internal investment teams were the leading source of direct investment opportunities for 77 per cent of APAC respondents, pointing to greater investment professionalisation within the region's family offices.

AI has emerged as the standout investment theme. Some 80 per cent of APAC family offices identified AI as a primary sector focus for direct investments, alongside interest in healthcare, robotics and software.
APAC family offices also showed the highest level of comfort with digital assets globally, with half reporting no significant barriers to adoption.
At the same time, financial stability and market volatility remain major concerns, cited by 53 per cent and 52 per cent of APAC respondents, respectively.

Bernard Wai, head of Asia for Integrated Client Solutions and Global Family Office at Citi Wealth, said the findings pointed to a maturing APAC family-office sector adopting increasingly institutional investment practices.
"Family offices across Asia Pacific have evolved to become increasingly sophisticated, requiring the talent, setup and governance for a sovereign wealth fund-like investment mindset.

"Whether it is expanding into direct investing programmes, leveraging AI interfaces, or executing cross-border tax-aware transactions, family offices here are taking a more holistic approach to wealth stewardship," he said.

Despite shifting macroeconomic indicators and geopolitical concerns, nearly 90 per cent of respondents reported positive portfolio performance year-to-date, while 41 per cent continue to target annual returns of 7.0 per cent to 10 per cent.
Public equities regained prominence, with nearly half of respondents increasing their exposure during the year, making the asset class the leading destination for new capital.

Private markets, meanwhile, remained a strategic component of family-office portfolios, although investors were becoming more selective and placing greater emphasis on sourcing, expertise and differentiated access.
The report also found that family offices are moving beyond experimentation with AI, deploying it for investment analysis, information management, reporting, workflow automation and decision support.

Rather than relying on AI to generate investment returns, family offices are primarily using the technology to improve productivity, speed up information processing and strengthen due diligence, while retaining human oversight of final decisions.
Citi said family wealth is increasingly international, with 38 per cent of respondents expecting family globalisation to rise in the next five years.

"With many respondents reporting assets, businesses and family members located across multiple jurisdictions, tax coordination, asset structuring, regulatory compliance and cross-border planning are becoming larger responsibilities for family offices.
"Building cross-border expertise will be essential as rising global complexity becomes a foundational aspect of family wealth," it said.

Citi also said succession is emerging as another immediate priority, with about one-third expecting leadership transitions within their family, family office or family business over the next five years.

The survey was launched at Citi Wealth's 11th Annual Family Office Leadership Summit in June, attended by more than 150 family-office leaders from over 25 countries, representing families with an average net worth of US$2.1 billion.

b0f0ffc42b09e2d5: TEHRAN, Oct 5 — Sebastien Ricci Iran’s top diplomat insisted yesterday that there would be no military solution to the United States’ war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

The main point of contention remains Iran’s attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker was struck by an unknown projectile.

“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
“There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions,” he continued, adding “only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict.

The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations.
Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.
The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it.

Yesterday the British maritime security agency UKMTO said a tanker in the Hormuz “reported being struck by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the engine room”, though the crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was recorded.
The agency did not specify the date of the incident, the vessel’s origin or destination, or whether it was an oil tanker or LNG carrier.
In Iran, oil minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned, the president’s office said on Sunday, as the US maintains a blockade on the country’s oil exports.

In a news bulletin on the minister’s resignation, state television ran an interview with an official from the Iranian presidential office who said Paknejad initially offered to quit a while ago “due to personal issues” but this was rejected.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had asked Paknejad to continue in his post but was now accepting his departure as the minister had insisted on leaving, the official added.
Paknejad has been replaced by Hamid Bovard, the chief executive of the National Iranian Oil Company, the presidency said.
Focused on Hormuz
Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.
Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.
Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Sunday that the US had expressed its views on the proposal and said they were being reviewed.

“The Americans, through intermediaries, have also conveyed their views on this proposal, and these views are currently being examined inside the country through the relevant channels and procedures,” he told reporters, according to state news agency IRNA.

“Whenever the final position of the Islamic Republic of Iran is ready, appropriate steps will be taken accordingly. At the same time, the Islamic Republic of Iran is also preparing itself for any other possible scenario.”
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday characterised the latest US counterproposal as being “in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues”.

“We have clearly indicated that we are focusing on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said, adding that reopening the waterway required “an end to the disruptions to Iranian commercial maritime traffic and the lifting of sanctions”.

The United States and Israel have said the war is necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons—a goal it has long denied pursuing—though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets.
The United States has not struck Iran since September 1, but it has recently pursued a fresh military buildup in the region. — AFP
f3e9ae0625a46e0f: NADI, Oct 5 — Extreme heat is putting pregnant mothers and their newborns at increasing risk, United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell will warn today.

Speaking at the “pre-COP” summit in Nadi, Fiji, Stiell will cite a new survey showing more than two thirds of health professionals across five continents had seen complications caused by intense heat in the past five years.
“Rising temperatures mean rising danger in pregnancy,” he is expected to say.
“Climate-driven extreme heat during pregnancy is increasingly linked to premature birth, stillbirth, low birth weight, and maternal complications.”
“The picture is clear and very disturbing: as extreme heat worsens, pregnancy and birth are now a new faultline in the global climate crisis, and one which is potentially fatal,” Stiell will say.
“This faultline must not become another deep chasm of climate-driven suffering, inequality and injustice.”
Scientists warn that climate change is making extreme weather events more intense and resulting in heat records tumbling more often.

Around 33 countries, spanning from western Europe to the Sahel and central America, recorded their hottest July since records began this year, according to AFP analysis of data from the European Union’s Copernicus climate observatory.
The survey of 1000 midwives and doctors in the United Kingdom, Australia, India, Brazil and Zimbabwe was commissioned by charitable foundation Wellcome.
Its chairwoman—Australian former Prime Minister Julia Gillard—said in a statement that mothers and babies are being put at increasing risk as a result of climate change.
“Extreme heat is an invisible killer, but pregnant women must not be invisible. Leaders have the evidence and solutions they need—now they must act,” Gillard said.
The survey found nearly all midwives and doctors had cared for mothers or babies suffering the effects of extreme heat.

About a third of respondents said they had seen cases of low birth weight or restricted growth, feeding difficulties, and dehydration or heat-related illness, all resulting from what they believed was extreme heat.
Stiell will tell pre-COP delegates that “pregnancy should be a time of hope”.
“But for millions, it is becoming a time of anxiety, as climate impacts fill everyday life with risk.”
The pre-COP31 summit in Fiji and the remote coral atoll Tuvalu is seen by Pacific leaders as a chance to draw attention to life on the frontline of climate change.
They are a precursor to the larger UN-sponsored global climate summit—known as COP31 -- to be held next month in Turkey. — AFP
3c133257776beb1a: PARIS, Oct 5 — Up to 500 schools across France will be totally or partly closed today because of a wave of student protests that has shaken the country, the education minister said.

Lessons will be “totally or partly suspended” in some “400-500” high schools as the security conditions “have not been fulfilled”, said Education Minister Edouard Geffray on Sunday, adding that 24 schools had been “burned or ransacked” since the start of the movement.
He described the closures as chiefly a security precaution ahead of large-scale protests that the leaders of the movement have called for Tuesday.

The teenagers at French high schools, known as lycees, say that their studies are being ruined by high teacher absence rates, overlong school days and dilapidated facilities, as well as other grievances.
Geffray said the number of schools affected on Monday would be comparable to the figure from Friday but vowed there would be a “partial, progressive return to lessons”.

More than a third of the 468 schools in the wider Ile-de-France region surrounding the capital will be shut today as a result of the protests, Valerie Pecresse, the right-wing president of the region, told broadcaster Franceinfo.

The movement began at a Paris school on September 17 but grew last week into nationwide protests marked in places by outbursts of violence involving teenagers and the security forces, which have used tear gas and truncheons against the students.
Deliberately targeted
At Saint-Denis, just north of Paris, students took turns expressing their grievances at an open-air meeting Sunday.
When you are a student from one of the deprived districts, said one student, “The violence is unleashed.”
She referred in particular to one student who had lost his teeth to a police rubber bullet and another who had been hit in the eye.
One 16-year-old boy, Campion, held a placard that read: “They say they are listening to us but prefer to gas us”.
“I don’t understand why the government deploys so much force against a case that is valid: our education, our future,” he told AFP.
Geffray, in his statement, spoke of far-left infiltrators who had “hijacked’ the movement “and engaged in extreme violence”.
“Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students,” he said, adding that 78 education staff members had been injured.
“They were deliberately targeted because they were employees of the national education system,” Geffray said.
Organisers have called for the protests to continue on Tuesday, citing a lack of “concrete measures” from the government.

In a bid to address the protesters’ concerns, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu set out a timetable on Sunday urging local authorities to prioritise filling gaps left by long-term absences and unfilled posts.
He also called a meeting for Tuesday with regional presidents to discuss overhauling the country’s often-dilapidated school buildings.
Violent incidents
More than 5,000 people, 85 percent of them minors, have been arrested since the start of the movement.

A 16-year-old was detained on Sunday over the assault of a teacher in the southern town of La Ciotat. The teacher, 59, was struck and doused with gasoline on the sidelines of a high school student protest on Friday.
A group of youths were last week filmed beating and kicking a policeman on the ground in Belfort in eastern France in images that caused an outcry among officials.
Two youths, Bulgarian nationals aged 15 and 17, have been arrested and investigated for suspected aggravated violence, the prosecutor said.
One of the youths, whom the policeman had tried to arrest before being beaten, has now filed his own attempted murder complaint, his lawyer said.
The France branch of Amnesty last week slammed “disproportionate police violence” in tackling the demonstrations and said students must be allowed to express their grievances.

“Authorities must allow young people to exercise these rights without fear of being hit by tear gas grenades or batons, or being arbitrarily taken into police custody,” said Amnesty France president Anne Savinel-Barras.

But Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated that security forces “are not cracking down on young people” but rather “protecting” school and university students wishing to “peacefully voice their demands”. — AFP
