129da104b2e14650: KUALA LUMPUR: The roar of Formula One engines at Sepang International Circuit (SIC) has reignited a global clamour for Malaysia's permanent return to the F1 calendar.
Fans and commentators online declared the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia one of the best races of the season and called on the sport's organisers to make a return.

Social media was flooded with tributes to the SIC in the hours after the chequered flag yesterday, with the overwhelming sentiment being that Malaysia should never have left the calendar and should not be allowed to leave again.
F1 commentator Matt Gallagher captured the mood succinctly in a post on X that drew more than 24,000 likes: "Petition to have Malaysia on the calendar every year till the end of time."

Motorsport outlet The Race leaned into the euphoria with a satirical "proposed 2027 F1 calendar" — listing all 24 grand prix weekends as being held in Malaysia, to the delight of fans who flooded the post with approving replies.
User @atrocidadcasera proposed a similar solution: "Listen all I'm saying is we could have many countries host their GPs in Malaysia.
"We could have the Spanish GP in Malaysia. We could have the Miami GP in Malaysia. We could even have the Monaco GP in Malaysia. Sepang, I love you."
Beyond the jokes, more measured voices made a substantive case for Sepang's return.
User Stefan wrote: "We need this track back on the calendar. Might have been the best race of the season so far? It's not just a drivers track, it's a racing track. So, so good.
"I hope the Malaysian government can work something out to make it financially viable, we need Sepang desperately."
User Paul McGinnes was equally effusive: "Now this... this is a proper race track. The 2026 Bahrain GP at the Sepang International Circuit, in Malaysia, was absolutely fantastic.
"It was a special event and the fans broke new records to attend it. I hope this isn't a one-off and that the Malaysian GP makes a return."
User Hunter wrote: "Malaysia should've never been taken off the calendar. I know it's a two-wheel-centred country but it's a great track and one of Tilke's (Hermann Tilke) finest creations.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government is actively discussing the possibility of having Malaysia back on the F1 calendar.
The Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was triggered by the war in the Middle East, rendering Bahrain and Saudi Arabia unsafe to host F1 races earlier in the season.
The 2026 event, held from Oct 2 to 4, was relocated from Bahrain to Sepang following an agreement involving the Malaysian and Bahrain governments, F1 and the FIA.
It was the first F1 race at SIC since 2017.
a3157e3f2c4101ab: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Food in the Klang Valley is often a fun adventure, allowing you to explore cuisine from a certain country or even a different state in Malaysia.
Think of it as a preview; if you like it, perhaps you can plan a holiday there to deep dive into the food and culture.
Like any adventure, one needs to shake things up a little rather than stick to familiar, conventional food choices.
Malay fare tends to be rather one-dimensional; if it’s not nasi lemak, nasi kerabu and perhaps nasi dagang, other dishes seem to find little space in our stomachs.
We’re not to blame as there’s an obvious skew for East Coast eats, probably because the ladies who often hold the F&B reins are more enterprising, expanding everywhere.
With their stronger flavours, it’s also no surprise they are everyone’s pick as seen by the long queues.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
You know you have walked into Kedah grounds as the restaurant is decorated with flags from Kedah. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
However, once in a while, it’s good to break away from that comfort zone, like exploring Kedah eats found in Restoran Langgaq, near the KL East area.
Since I was new to the place, I sneakily observed everyone’s orders to gauge the top favourites.
A family of four was seen sharing plate of Nasi Daging and the Bihun Sup Daging between their two young sons.

Some ordered the Mee Goreng or Pek Nga Kelapa, which are coconut pancakes, eaten dipped in sambal or gulai termenun — a kembung fish curry made famous in Kuala Kedah where fresh catch is cooked in a spicy curry.
Their pancakes aren’t the pale-looking lempeng usually found in the area; instead, they are aggressively pan-fried in a smoky pan until the edges brown.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
After frying the snacks, the Cucur Udang is left on the rack to allow excess oil to drip off. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
And the must-try item is their Cucur Udang Biasa, known as Coq Udang in Kedah dialect, served piping hot.

Limited stomach space meant a leaner meal this round: just two dishes and a snack but each item was satisfying enough to warrant a return visit to explore more items like their packets of nasi kuning, Kedah’s colourful answer to nasi lemak with different gulai, mee rebus, mee goreng and laksa.
Nasi Daging (RM13) arrives on a stainless steel plate: brown-coloured rice topped with boiled beef slices, served with three small bowls containing beef broth, dalca tetel and ayaq asam kerisek.
The rice is cooked in beef stock with spices like star anise, cloves, cardamom pods and cinnamon sticks, and layered with fresh coriander leaves on top.
The meat is quite lean but still pulls apart easily, while the dalca tetel adds a layer of curry flavour too.

On its own, the rice and beef have a mild beefy flavour but once you eat it with the ayaq asam kerisek, a dip with tamarind, chopped chilies, and onions, it’s an appetising combination that will have you cleaning up every rice grain from the plate.
Depending on your budget, you can order a more decadent tulang rusuk (a long beef rib) and those who enjoy offal can also add beef tripe and cow lungs.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Bihun Sup Daging may look small but it’s big on beef flavour with the boiled meat cut into slices and a robust beef broth. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
Bihun Sup Daging (RM13) arrives with an impressive blanket of beef slices in a small bowl.
As you dig underneath it, there’s yellow-tinged vermicelli and piping hot beef broth that calls immediately to be enjoyed before the temperature drops.
It’s a lighter meal that balances out the more substantial Nasi Daging, giving you much needed space for their famous Cucur Udang (RM13).
This is prepared from noon onwards at the cooking station in front, allowing you to view the theatrics of making the prawn fritters.
A scoop of the yellow tinged batter, mixed with matchsticks of cucumber and yam bean is topped with small raw prawns still in their shells.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Cucur Udang is done differently here, starting with a ladle of batter (left) dotted with shreds of cucumber and yam bean that is topped with fresh prawns, which is then poured into hot oil (right) at the edge of the hot wok. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi

Rather than frying it in the ladle to create a saucer shaped fritter, they quickly tilt the batter into the hot oil at the edge of the wok, allowing the batter to feather out into a larger, thinner, and crunchier piece.
As the fritter clings to the side of the wok, they slowly scrape it out once it’s partially fried, allowing the entire piece to hit the hot oil.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This frying method sees thin crispy crackers clinging to the side of the wok in hot oil. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
They continue frying it on both sides until it becomes golden brown, ensuring the fritter is crispy.
Any excess oil is shaken away and the fritter is placed on a metal rack for any extra oil to drip out.
Once cooled, the huge fritter is chopped into smaller, manageable pieces, to be dipped not in chili sauce but in a thick, chunky peanut sauce.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Move aside chili sauce, peanut sauce makes for a better pairing with the crunchy golden fritter. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
On the side, there are also cubes of cucumber, yam bean and fried beancurd.
It’s best eaten on the spot otherwise its texture will be compromised.
Restoran Langgaq
6, Jalan 4/4C, Desa Melawati,
Kuala Lumpur
Open: 8am to 11pm. Closed on Mondays.

ee1405955a1b254e: PETALING JAYA: There are moments in sport when the person celebrating has as much reason to smile as the champion standing on the podium.
For Nicol David, that moment came in Nagoya when Ng Eain Yow and S Sivasangari became the first squash players to secure qualification places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
She was there to witness it, sharing the joy of two Malaysians who had achieved something she spent years fighting to make possible.

For much of her career, Nicol carried squash’s Olympic dream around the world, appearing in campaign videos, making presentations and helping persuade the International Olympic Committee (IOC) that her sport belonged at the Games.
Now, two compatriots had walked through the door she helped open.
There was something wonderfully fitting about that.
Nicol, an eight-time world champion and former world No 1 for 108 consecutive months, once famously said she would trade all her world titles for an Olympic gold medal.
She retired in 2019 without getting the chance to compete for one. Squash had missed out on the 2020 and 2024 Olympics before the IOC finally approved its inclusion in October 2023.
The woman who had fought so hard for that recognition could now watch a new generation pursue the prize that had eluded her.
But this was not simply a story about Nicol’s dream. Eain Yow and Sivasangari had to earn their moment, and they did so in style.
Both arrived in Nagoya as defending Asian Games champions, carrying the expectations that come with having already tasted gold.

Eain Yow defeated India’s Abhay Singh 11-9, 11-5, 11-5 to retain the men's singles title. Sivasangari followed with an equally assured 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 victory over India’s Anahat Singh in the women’s final.

Their victories delivered Malaysia's fifth and sixth gold medals at the Games, meeting the national contingent’s original target. More importantly, they secured the first two squash qualification places for LA28.
For Sivasangari, the achievement carried a particularly personal meaning.
Four years earlier, she had survived a serious road accident that left her with neck and spinal injuries. There were questions about whether she would walk again, let alone return to elite sport.
Yet there she was, defending her Asian Games crown and securing an Olympic place.
Her victory over Anahat was a composed display from a player who understood the occasion without allowing it to overwhelm her.
Afterwards, she described Olympic qualification as a dream come true, while making clear that she wanted to keep improving.
There is something lovely about that combination: the joy of reaching a destination and the hunger to go further.
Eain Yow was equally clear about what comes next.
“I want to be world number one, I want to be world champion, and I want an Olympic gold medal,” he said after Malaysia’s men’s team victory.
“I want it all in this sport, so I will keep working hard.”
It was an ambitious declaration, but one that captured what Olympic inclusion means for squash. Players can now pursue an Olympic medal alongside world titles and professional rankings.
The celebrations did not end with the singles finals.
Malaysia went on to collect two more squash gold medals, finishing with four golds and one bronze. No other individual sport contributed as many gold medals to the national tally at Aichi-Nagoya.

The women's team retained its title with a 2-1 victory over Hong Kong China. Aifa Azman gave Malaysia the opening point before Sivasangari lost a five-game battle to Chan Sin Yuk. Aira Azman then settled the contest with an 11-9, 11-5, 11-4 win over Lee Ka Yi.

The victory was another reminder that team gold is rarely the work of one player. Aifa and Aira, sisters sharing the court and the responsibility, helped deliver a triumph that demanded composure after Hong Kong had drawn level.
The men's team provided another memorable finish, defeating Pakistan 2-0 to reclaim the title last won by Malaysia in 2018.
Ameeshenraj Chandaran recovered from losing the opening game to beat Nasir Iqbal 8-11, 11-3, 11-6, 11-4.
Eain Yow then had to dig deep against Noor Zaman, recovering from a two-game deficit to win 11-8, 6-11, 7-11, 11-4, 11-5.

For Eain Yow, the team triumph also settled unfinished business. He had delivered the winning point when Malaysia won gold at the 2018 Asian Games, but the team managed only bronze in Hangzhou four years later.
His joy was not simply about adding another medal to his collection. It was about helping his teammates reclaim a title they had lost.
That is the part of sport a medal table cannot quite capture: the shared memories, the disappointments carried forward and the satisfaction of finally getting it right together.
The significance of the remarkable squash campaign reaches beyond the medals.

Olympic inclusion gives squash a new platform to reach children who might never otherwise have considered picking up a racket. It also offers national associations a stronger case for funding, better facilities and pathways for young players.
Nicol has long spoken about the opportunities Olympic recognition could bring to participation and the sport’s future.

For Malaysia, the opportunity comes with a proud history. Nicol, Ong Beng Hee and generations of players helped establish the country's standing in world squash. Eain Yow and Sivasangari are now carrying that tradition into a new chapter.
They still have work to do before Los Angeles, but they can prepare knowing that the sport they love will finally have its place on the Olympic stage.

And somewhere in that journey is Nicol, whose playing career ended before squash received its Olympic invitation, but whose efforts helped ensure that others would not have to wonder what might have been.
A champion's legacy is often measured by the titles she wins, the records she leaves behind and the players who follow in her footsteps.
Nicol has all of those.
Now she has something else: the sight of two Malaysians beginning an Olympic journey that once seemed beyond the reach of their sport.
When the opening ball is struck in Los Angeles, Malaysia will have every reason to cheer.
Eain Yow and Sivasangari will carry their own ambitions, but they will also carry the history of a sport that fought for the right to be there.
And perhaps, amid the excitement, they will remember the woman who stood in Nagoya to share their joy.
Some dreams are fulfilled by the people who first imagine them. Others find their meaning in the lives they make possible.
For this one, a simple thank you will do.
Thank you, Nicol.
8ccacbe374341cad: PETALING JAYA: Dalam dunia sukan, ada waktunya insan yang berdiri di tepi gelanggang mempunyai sebab yang sama besarnya untuk tersenyum seperti juara yang berada di atas podium.
Bagi Nicol David, detik itu hadir di Nagoya apabila Ng Eain Yow dan S Sivasangari menjadi dua pemain skuasy pertama meraih slot ke Olimpik Los Angeles 2028 (LA28).
Nicol berada di sana menyaksikan sendiri sejarah tercipta, berkongsi kegembiraan dengan dua rakyat Malaysia yang kini berpeluang mengejar sesuatu yang beliau perjuangkan selama bertahun-tahun.
Sepanjang sebahagian besar kerjayanya, Nicol membawa impian skuasy untuk menjadi sukan Olimpik ke merata dunia.
Beliau muncul dalam video kempen, membuat pembentangan dan membantu meyakinkan Jawatankuasa Olimpik Antarabangsa (IOC) bahawa skuasy layak berada di temasya terbesar dunia itu.
Kini, dua rakan senegaranya bakal melangkah ke pentas yang beliau sendiri bantu buka.
Seolah-olah semuanya melengkapkan sebuah perjalanan yang panjang.

Nicol, juara dunia lapan kali yang pernah menghuni ranking nombor satu dunia selama 108 bulan berturut-turut, pernah berkata beliau sanggup menukar semua gelaran dunianya demi satu pingat emas Olimpik.
Namun, beliau bersara pada 2019 tanpa pernah mendapat peluang itu. Skuasy gagal disenaraikan untuk Olimpik 2020 dan 2024 sebelum IOC akhirnya meluluskan penyertaannya bagi LA28 pada Oktober 2023.
Wanita yang sekian lama memperjuangkan pengiktirafan itu kini boleh menyaksikan generasi baharu mengejar hadiah yang tidak pernah sempat berada dalam genggamannya.
Tetapi kisah ini bukan sekadar tentang impian Nicol.
Eain Yow dan Sivasangari sendiri perlu berjuang mendapatkan tempat mereka, dan kedua-duanya melakukannya dengan penuh bergaya.
Mereka tiba di Nagoya sebagai juara bertahan Sukan Asia, sekali gus memikul tekanan dan harapan yang datang selepas pernah merasai nikmat berada di puncak.
Eain Yow mempertahankan emas perseorangan lelaki dengan menewaskan pemain India, Abhay Singh, 11-9, 11-5, 11-5.
Sivasangari pula tampil sama meyakinkan apabila menundukkan seorang lagi wakil India, Anahat Singh, 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 dalam final wanita.
Kemenangan mereka menghadiahkan emas kelima dan keenam Malaysia di temasya itu, sekali gus memenuhi sasaran asal kontinjen negara.
Lebih besar daripada itu, kejayaan berkenaan turut menghadiahkan dua slot kelayakan pertama skuasy ke LA28.
Bagi Sivasangari, kejayaan itu membawa makna yang jauh lebih peribadi.
Empat tahun lalu, beliau terselamat daripada kemalangan jalan raya serius yang menyebabkan kecederaan pada leher dan tulang belakang.
Ketika itu, timbul persoalan sama ada beliau mampu berjalan seperti biasa semula, apatah lagi kembali bersaing di peringkat tertinggi.
Namun di Nagoya, Sivasangari bukan sahaja kembali berdiri di gelanggang malah mempertahankan gelaran Sukan Asia dan memastikan dirinya mempunyai tempat di pentas Olimpik.
Menentang Anahat, beliau tampil tenang dan terkawal, memahami besarnya makna perlawanan itu tanpa membiarkan tekanan menguasainya.
Selepas kemenangan itu, Sivasangari menyifatkan kelayakan Olimpik sebagai impian menjadi kenyataan, tetapi pada masa sama menegaskan masih banyak ruang untuk dirinya menjadi pemain lebih baik.
Di situlah indahnya perjalanan seorang atlet: meraikan sebuah destinasi yang akhirnya dicapai sambil masih dahagakan perjalanan seterusnya.
Eain Yow juga jelas dengan apa yang diinginkannya selepas ini.
“Saya mahu menjadi pemain nombor satu dunia, saya mahu menjadi juara dunia dan saya mahu pingat emas Olimpik,” katanya selepas kemenangan skuad lelaki Malaysia.
“Saya mahukan semuanya dalam sukan ini, jadi saya akan terus bekerja keras.”
Ia satu cita-cita besar, tetapi kata-kata itu menggambarkan betapa pentingnya kemasukan skuasy ke Olimpik.
Buat pertama kali, pemain skuasy bukan sahaja boleh memburu gelaran dunia dan ranking profesional, malah kini mempunyai pingat Olimpik sebagai kemuncak impian.
Dan pesta skuasy Malaysia di Nagoya tidak terhenti selepas final perseorangan.
Malaysia kemudian menambah dua lagi emas menerusi acara berpasukan untuk menamatkan kempen skuasy dengan empat emas dan satu gangsa.
Tiada sukan individu lain menyumbang emas sebanyak itu kepada kontinjen negara di Aichi-Nagoya.
Skuad wanita mempertahankan gelaran selepas menewaskan Hong Kong China 2-1.
Aifa Azman memberikan mata pertama kepada Malaysia sebelum Sivasangari tewas dalam pertarungan lima set kepada Chan Sin Yuk.
Dengan kedudukan terikat, Aira Azman muncul menamatkan cabaran lawan menerusi kemenangan 11-9, 11-5, 11-4 ke atas Lee Ka Yi.
Ia sekali lagi membuktikan emas berpasukan jarang sekali menjadi hasil usaha seorang pemain sahaja.
Aifa dan Aira, dua beradik yang berkongsi gelanggang serta tanggungjawab membawa nama negara, membantu memastikan Malaysia kekal tenang selepas Hong Kong menyamakan kedudukan.
Skuad lelaki pula menghadiahkan satu lagi penamat manis apabila menewaskan Pakistan 2-0 untuk merampas semula gelaran yang kali terakhir dimenangi Malaysia pada 2018.
Ameeshenraj Chandaran bangkit selepas tewas set pertama untuk menundukkan Nasir Iqbal 8-11, 11-3, 11-6, 11-4.
Eain Yow kemudian terpaksa bekerja lebih keras menentang Noor Zaman.
Selepas ketinggalan 1-2, beliau bangkit untuk menang 11-8, 6-11, 7-11, 11-4, 11-5 dan memastikan emas menjadi milik Malaysia.
Buat Eain Yow, kejayaan itu turut menutup satu urusan yang belum selesai.
Beliau pernah menyumbang mata kemenangan ketika Malaysia meraih emas di Sukan Asia 2018, tetapi empat tahun kemudian di Hangzhou, skuad negara sekadar membawa pulang gangsa.
Kegembiraannya kali ini bukan sekadar kerana menambah satu lagi pingat dalam koleksi peribadi.
Ia tentang membantu rakan sepasukannya mendapatkan kembali gelaran yang pernah terlepas daripada tangan mereka.

Itulah sisi sukan yang tidak mampu diceritakan sepenuhnya oleh jadual pingat: kenangan yang dikongsi bersama, kekecewaan yang dibawa bertahun-tahun dan kepuasan apabila akhirnya semuanya menjadi seperti diharapkan.
Namun, makna kejayaan luar biasa skuasy Malaysia di Nagoya melangkaui pingat.
Kehadiran skuasy di Olimpik memberi sukan itu pentas baharu untuk mendekati kanak-kanak yang mungkin tidak pernah terfikir untuk memegang raket.
Ia juga memberi persatuan kebangsaan alasan lebih kukuh untuk mendapatkan dana, membina kemudahan lebih baik dan menyediakan laluan pembangunan lebih jelas kepada pemain muda.
Nicol sejak sekian lama bercakap tentang peluang yang boleh dibuka menerusi pengiktirafan Olimpik, bukan sahaja kepada pemain elit tetapi juga masa depan skuasy secara keseluruhan.
Bagi Malaysia, peluang itu hadir bersama sejarah yang membanggakan.
Nicol, Ong Beng Hee dan generasi pemain sebelum ini membantu membina nama Malaysia dalam skuasy dunia.
Kini, Eain Yow dan Sivasangari membawa legasi itu memasuki lembaran baharu.
Masih banyak kerja menanti sebelum mereka tiba di Los Angeles.
Tetapi sekurang-kurangnya kali ini, mereka boleh membuat persiapan dengan mengetahui sukan yang dicintai akhirnya mempunyai tempat di pentas Olimpik.
Dan di suatu sudut perjalanan itu ada Nicol.

Kerjaya permainannya berakhir sebelum skuasy menerima jemputan ke Olimpik, tetapi perjuangannya membantu memastikan generasi selepasnya tidak perlu lagi tertanya-tanya bagaimana rasanya jika peluang itu pernah diberikan.
Legasi seorang juara selalunya diukur melalui gelaran yang dimenangi, rekod yang ditinggalkan dan pemain yang meneruskan jejak langkahnya.
Nicol memiliki semua itu.
Kini, beliau mempunyai sesuatu yang lain.
Beliau dapat menyaksikan sendiri dua rakyat Malaysia memulakan perjalanan Olimpik yang suatu ketika dahulu terasa begitu jauh daripada jangkauan skuasy.
Apabila bola pertama dipukul di Los Angeles nanti, Malaysia mempunyai banyak sebab untuk bersorak.
Eain Yow dan Sivasangari akan membawa impian mereka sendiri, tetapi bersama mereka turut terbawa sejarah sebuah sukan yang berjuang begitu lama untuk mendapat tempat di sana.
Dan mungkin di tengah-tengah keterujaan itu, mereka akan mengenang wanita yang berdiri bersama mereka di Nagoya untuk berkongsi kegembiraan.
Ada impian yang tercapai dalam tangan insan yang mula-mula membayangkannya.
Ada juga impian yang menemukan maknanya apabila ia membuka jalan untuk orang lain.
Untuk impian yang satu ini, mungkin dua perkataan sudah memadai.
Terima kasih, Nicol.
172a08a3c963bad9: PETALING JAYA: For the first three months of Rayhan’s life, his mother had no idea anything was seriously wrong. He seemed like any other baby, with nothing to prepare her for the diagnosis that would follow.

Then came a worrying spell of illness. Rayhan vomited for a week, his tummy became swollen, and he struggled to go to the toilet normally. Blood tests were carried out as doctors investigated what was happening to her little boy.

He was eventually diagnosed with hydranencephaly, a rare condition in which most of the brain’s cerebral hemispheres are absent. His mother now faces questions about his health and a future she had never expected.
Rayhan is two today, and his mum’s wishes for him are simple. “I just want him to be able to sit up, walk, and be healthy. That’s what any mother would want,” she shared in a video.
As a single mother, she is trying to give him the care he needs while keeping up with living expenses. His special milk formula alone uses up a substantial share of the money available.
“Four boxes of milk powder already cost RM600. Then I still have to pay rent, electricity and water ... it’s all money. It’s very difficult," she expressed.

Rayhan's best chances of treatment require them to travel to Penang for further specialist assessment. For his mother, getting him there from their home in Kedah means finding money for each journey while making sure there is still enough for his daily needs.

Thankfully, they now have the support of Pusat Kebajikan VCare Kuala Muda, which has stepped in to help raise the funds required. The welfare NGO hopes to collect approximately RM16,000 to ease the pressure on his mother and help Rayhan receive medical attention and everyday care.

The funds will cover examinations, specialist assessments and treatment, together with formula milk, nutritional support, diapers and other necessities. They will also help with transport between Kedah and Penang.

There are still decisions ahead about Rayhan’s treatment. Specialists must assess his brain scans and physical condition before determining whether surgery could help manage complications involving the fluid around his brain.

No treatment can replace the brain tissue that is missing, and surgery cannot promise the milestones his mother longs for. But medical care can address complications and support his comfort, while reliable access to milk and supplies can make a difference to his daily life.

For his mother, these everyday needs continue between appointments: her little boy still needs to be fed, changed and cared for, and she still has household bills to meet. VCare welcomes contributions of any amount to help pay for the things that have become such a source of worry.
His mother cannot know what Rayhan will eventually be able to do. But she wants to give him every opportunity to receive the support he needs.
A helping hand now would allow her to spend less time worrying about how to afford it, and more time simply being there for her child.
If you wish to help, send your contribution to Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) account 0219 0411 0012 2711 (Persatuan Kebajikan VCare Kuala Muda).
Please use the reference ‘CASE51’ or ‘RAYHAN’. For confirmation of your donation, send them a WhatsApp message with the transaction slip.
For further information, contact Jeanna Goh at 016-337 2749. Find out more about Persatuan Kebajikan VCare Kuala Muda here.

2878b624975f40cc: KUALA TERENGGANU: A retiree in his 70s lost RM367,950 in savings and proceeds from a land sale after falling victim to an online investment scam involving a woman he befriended on WhatsApp.
Kuala Terengganu police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim lodged a police report at 11.49am yesterday.
He said the victim was first contacted on July 31 by a woman identifying herself as "Via", who claimed she had messaged him by mistake, believing he was a contractor named "Mahdir".
"Through their subsequent interactions, the suspect developed a close relationship with the victim and offered him an opportunity to join an investment scheme to generate income.
"To gain his trust, the victim received returns from his first three transactions, convincing him that the scheme was legitimate," he said.
Azli said the suspect subsequently instructed the victim to transfer investment capital in stages to several bank accounts allegedly serving as intermediaries for the scheme.
Between Aug 22 and Sept 30, the victim made 72 transactions involving 13 accounts, transferring a total of RM367,950.
However, he received no further returns.
The victim was later told that his accumulated capital and profits on the platform had exceeded RM800,000 and were ready for withdrawal.
"However, when he attempted to withdraw the money, the main platform operator claimed there was an issue with his account, citing an 'abnormal relationship between funds and tax'.
"The operator then demanded an additional RM80,765 as a processing fee before the funds could be released," Azli said.
He said the victim refused to pay after suspecting that the operator was deliberately imposing additional charges and making excuses to prevent him from withdrawing his money.
The victim then lodged a police report.
Azli said the money lost comprised the victim's personal savings and proceeds from a recent land sale.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.

fc3dca6f57fb264d: BEIJING, Oct 5 — Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open yesterday beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.
The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite.
Djokovic called it one of his best matches of the year, alongside his epic five-set win over Italy’s Jannik Sinner to reach the final at the Australian Open.
He told reporters such battles were “evidence to me that I can still beat the best players in the world on the biggest stage”.
“Things are a bit different nowadays. It’s hard to be consistently playing on the highest level like the youngsters,” he said.
He needed to play a mix of shots in “high-risk tennis” against the German, but he said feeling “physically pretty good” on the court after dealing all year with health issues helped him fight back.
Djokovic got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.
Boos filled the stadium soon afterward when the umpire agreed to replay a point Djokovic had won, after Zverev complained about a flicker in the LED panels during play.
The German saw out the first set from there, but a valiant Djokovic roared back to seal the second with a cross-court winner to break serve and force a decider.
The 24-time Grand Slam champion faced 19 Zverev aces throughout the match but held steady on his own serve to go 5-4 ahead in the final set.
He then broke the world number two to take the set and the match, seemingly defying his recent physical difficulties with victory in a gruelling two hours and 34 minutes.
Djokovic will face Medvedev in the final four after the former world number one dispatched Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7/4), 6-3.
Poland’s Hubert Hurkacz also advanced to the semi-finals after beating Karen Khachanov, and will play Australia’s Alex de Minaur, who survived a gruelling test to beat Andrey Rublev 1-6, 6-2, 6-3.
Sabalenka swept out
Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets in the third round, leaving the women’s draw without its top two seeds.
Czech player Nikola Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.
“I focused on myself, to be calm,” 34th-ranked Bartunkova said.
“She’s a legend... so I’m really happy that I won the match,” she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.
Bartunkova next faces Austria’s Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.
A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.
Top seed Elena Rybakina—who replaced Sabalenka as world number one weeks ago—is also out, having lost to Alina Charaeva in the second round.
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva of Russia set up a fourth-round match with Ukraine’s Daria Snigur, while Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova breezed past Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1.
Noskova next faces 28th-ranked Russian player Ekaterina Alexandrova.
Naomi Osaka, the 2019 champion, beat Sara Bejlek and will face either Karolina Muchova or Liudmila Samsonova, scheduled to play each other. — AFP
248a7e8455be84b4: LONDON, Oct 5 — Harry Kane said England’s 7-0 rout of Croatia in the Nations League served as a statement of intent to their European rivals.
Thomas Tuchel’s side ran riot in Rijeka on Saturday thanks to Kane’s double and a brace from Bukayo Saka.
Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers were also on target for the Three Lions in the biggest win of Tuchel’s reign.
Bayern Munich striker Kane, who has 89 goals from 124 internationals, believes the dynamic performance served a blueprint for England as they build towards co-hosting Euro 2028.
It was a stark contrast to England’s meek surrender when Tuchel adopted a defensive game plan in the closing stages of their World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina in July.
“Even when we were 1-0 up, we went for two, went for three, went for four, and that’s got to be our mentality,” Kane said.
“When you have a certain style of playing, you can’t just pick and choose when you want to do it. It’s just relentless. It’s non-stop.
“You get four, you want five. You go and have a really hungry mentality.
“That’s needed to change, especially in the bigger games, in the bigger tournaments, and these games will only help us.”
Inflicting Croatia’s heaviest ever defeat, England showed the pace, poise and movement that went missing in the latter stages of the World Cup.
Kane is convinced England’s ability to put Croatia to the sword showed they are not to be underestimated by the other top sides in Europe.
“We’re playing against a really good side. We can’t take this type of win for granted because it could have been a really tricky game for us,” the England captain said.
“And it’s always just sending messages - not just to yourself, but to the other teams around Europe. I think we’ve done that again.
“We’re hungry. We’re a young team. We have players in amazing form right now, and I think everyone’s just excited to be out there on the pitch.
“Performances like this will only make us more motivated.”
Kane is set to become England’s joint highest-capped player on Tuesday against Czech Republic at Wembley when he will draw level with Peter Shilton on 125 caps.
The 33-year-old also has another target in his sights as he is 11 away from a century of international goals.
“It’s coming. It’s 89 now, so obviously, it’s getting closer and closer,” he said.
“We have a special game on Tuesday in terms of the caps, obviously 100 goals is a nice round number and it would be incredible to reach, of course.” — AFP
8eb1df08cad46308: SEPANG, Oct 5 — Formula One’s lawmakers have vowed to launch a full investigation into the rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix, which Lewis Hamilton likened to a “Lego race” after multiple cars broke down with software problems, reported PA Media/dpa.
Max Verstappen navigated his way through the chaos to claim his first triumph of the year.
Kimi Antonelli took second, with Lewis Hamilton completing a fine comeback drive from 18th to finish on the podium.
George Russell retired from third with an engine issue, leaving his world championship dream all but over.

However, the race at the Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia was overshadowed by embarrassing and unprecedented scenes when this season’s new cars — which have already faced stern criticism — effectively failed to work in the wet.
The initial getaway had already been pushed back by 40 minutes following a deluge of rain.

F1 bosses then had to abandon the start when a number of drivers, including Verstappen and Hamilton, were struck by gremlins on the formation lap, with problems linked to the controversial 50-50 split between combustion and battery power leaving them unable to get their cars to operate.
Pole-sitter Verstappen was the first to complain that he could not accelerate. His crawling pace had a knock-on effect, with Hamilton, running behind Verstappen, then hitting trouble in his Ferrari.
“I am pressing the throttle, and nothing is happening,” said Hamilton before stopping at the side of the track.
A whole host of other drivers were also struggling to keep their engines running in the first meaningful wet running for this generation of car.
Verstappen, who has threatened to quit the sport because of his disdain of the new regulations, was eventually able to get up to speed.
He laughed and shook his head upon seeing some of the cars parked at the side of the track.
“Look at this,” he said over the radio.
The grid eventually limped back to the pit lane, and a further 53 minutes passed before the green light was given by the sport’s chiefs to restart the race.
An explanation for the lengthy delay was not offered at the time, although it later emerged that new software had to be downloaded to the cars.
Two laps then followed behind the safety car before a standing start.
Verstappen took the chequered flag 2.3 seconds clear of Antonelli.
“These engines are so complicated, and a lot of software is implemented,” said Verstappen as he reflected on the chaos that puts the sport’s contentious rules firmly back in the spotlight.
“I triggered it first, and then I looked in my mirror, and I was like, ‘Wait, are they waiting for me?’”
Hamilton, sitting next to Verstappen in the post-race news conference, said: “It was like the Lego race (before the British Grand Prix).”
Verstappen continued: “What can you say? That’s not what you want for the sport.”
Hamilton added: “I had to stop on track and stop the car and engine and restart it. I’ve never done that before. I hope there is a lesson learned.”

The FIA said in a statement on Sunday: “On the formation lap an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars.

“As a result, the FIA Technical Department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain, enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race.

“This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue.”
Russell’s failure to finish leaves him 84 points behind his team-mate with only seven scheduled races and a possible 183 points remaining.
“The whole day felt like a bit of a faff, with the delay, the red flag, and endless laps behind the safety car,” he said.
“It didn’t feel very ‘F1’ today. And I would have been disappointed if I was in the stands and watching that unfold.” — Bernama-PA Media/dpa
*Editor’s note: The initials FIA stands for Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile, the international governing body for motorsport.
ca8f4455ee360a49: sBUENOS AIRES, (Argentina):
Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions.

After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain's armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina's emerging generation.
The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima.
Messi also bows out as Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.
His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina's ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression.
"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
- Friends reunited -

Members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad — the players who delivered the country's third star — and their families will join Messi for Tuesday's farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world.

de2b70af458341ba: PORTO, Oct 5 — Portugal defeated Norway 2-1 without sulking superstar striker Cristiano Ronaldo yesterday to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals.
Goncalo Ramos secured a comeback victory for Jorge Jesus’s Portugal in the Group A4 clash after Joao Cancelo’s rocket levelled Kristoffer Ajer’s stunning opener for Norway.

Portugal played out the final minutes with 10 men after Francisco Conceicao was dismissed for two yellow cards in the space of a few seconds for dissent after he appealed for a penalty unsuccessfully.

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United striker Ronaldo walked out on the squad on Wednesday ahead of the previous game against Denmark, after Portugal’s all-time top goalscorer learned he would not start.
Portugal are now guaranteed to finish in the top two spots in the group with two matches to spare, thus becoming the first team to reach the last eight in March 2027.
“Cristiano is our captain, the best player Portugal has ever had,” Cancelo told RTP.
“Things will certainly end in the best way (with Ronaldo) but the important thing is the four victories.”
Norway took the lead in Porto against the run of play with a stunning effort from Brentford defender Ajer after 36 minutes.
The Norwegian met a bouncing ball on the edge of the box perfectly to bend it into the top corner.
However two minutes later Barcelona defender Cancelo scored a similarly superb goal, rifling home from around 20 yards.
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland fired across the face of goal after an hour and was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen a few minutes later.
Nations League holders and two-time record champions Portugal nosed in front when AC Milan striker Ramos, starting in place of Ronaldo, tucked home from close range.
Ramos was teed up by Joao Felix, who reached Vitinha’s lofted pass and put it on a plate for the forward.
Ramos scored for a third consecutive game, and helped Portugal seal back-to-back wins since 41-year-old forward Ronaldo left the squad.

Conceicao’s foolish dismissal left Jesus’s team in a tough spot for the final few minutes. The Juventus winger was about to be replaced by Pedro Neto but his complaints led to a red card before the substitution could happen.
Portugal held on to triumph for the fourth time in four games in the group, completing a successful first international window for 72-year-old coach Jesus, despite the Ronaldo controversy.
“Any player who comes to the national team is welcome, obviously. If Cris returns, we’ll be here to receive him with open arms,” said Portugal defender Nuno Mendes. — AFP
a39e6cecdb0ed673: PORTO, Oct 5 — Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the squad if he wishes, despite walking out on his team-mates, said national team coach Jorge Jesus yesterday.
Jesus said Ronaldo can come back into the fold “if he wants to” after the team beat Norway without the veteran attacker to reach the Nations League quarter-finals.

The dispute began last week when Jesus left 41-year-old Ronaldo on the bench for Portugal’s first win over Norway. Ronaldo subsequently walked out on the squad on Wednesday after learning he would not start against Denmark.

“For me, Cris, in the next call-up, if he’s playing at Al-Nassr, he’ll be a player who can be called up,” Jesus told reporters, referring to Ronaldo’s Saudi club side. “If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team.”
The coach said if Ronaldo wishes to speak to him before Portugal’s next matches in November, that would happen.
“If he wants to, as we did before this call-up, we talked before the call-up, we can talk before the next call-up,” continued Jesus. “But Cris is the one who’s going to decide.”
Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo is Portugal’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.
Jesus said he had told Ronaldo he needed him in the squad for his first games at the helm after replacing Roberto Martinez following the 2026 World Cup.
“Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants, he’s the one who will decide how he wants it,” said Jesus.

“That’s how we talked, the two of us—I said, ‘I need you’. In my first call-up, I said, ‘I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you’. And now I’m saying the same thing.”
Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football.
The forward has been a fixture of the national team for more than two decades and has played at six World Cups.
In Ronaldo’s absence Portugal became the first team to secure a place in the quarter-finals, with two group games still to play.
Ronaldo’s long-time rival for the title of the world’s best player, Lionel Messi, will play his final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires on Tuesday. — AFP
5eb1801398eab24c: LONDON: Harry Kane is set to equal England's appearance record with his 125th cap against the Czech Republic on Tuesday as the striker looks to build on his flourishing partnership with "scary" Jude Bellingham.
Kane will take centre stage if he ties former England goalkeeper Peter Shilton's landmark in the Nations League clash at Wembley.
The England captain's pride in representing his country has shone through since his debut against Lithuania in 2015.
Kane scored within two minutes of coming off the bench in that match, and he has rarely endured a barren spell in an England shirt ever since.
The 33-year-old is England's record scorer with 89 goals after netting twice in Saturday's 7-0 demolition of Croatia.
Bayern Munich star Kane has been England's talisman and the one constant throughout their highs and lows over the last 11 years.
Roy Hodgson gave Kane his England debut and the striker has since played under coaches Sam Allardyce, Gareth Southgate, Lee Carsley and now Thomas Tuchel.
But even having a player of Kane's predatory instincts and remarkable consistency has not been enough for England to end their angst-ridden wait for a first major trophy since the 1966 World Cup.
England lost the European Championship final in 2021 and 2024.

And for Kane to follow Bobby Moore as the only male England captain to lift a trophy, Tuchel believes he needs an assist from a midfielder whose virtuoso performance against Croatia on Saturday drew gushing praise from team-mates and pundits alike.

In danger of missing out on the World Cup after being dropped from the England squad in October 2025, Real Madrid star Bellingham has gone from Tuchel's doghouse to the penthouse over the last 12 months.
Having irked Tuchel with his volatile on-pitch antics, Bellingham eventually regained his place in time for the World Cup in June and July.
It was Bellingham rather than Kane who finished as England's top scorer at the World Cup, but their tournament ended in semi-final heartbreak against Argentina.
'Never seen anything like it'
Tuchel's defensive tactics in the closing stage of that loss were widely pilloried.
But has learnt from that late meltdown and wants England to stay on the offensive, with Kane and Bellingham leading the charge.
Key to England's hopes of winning Euro 2028 will be Kane staying healthy and Bellingham remaining in the kind of masterful form that inspired the rout of Croatia.

The 23-year-old was so dominant in Rijeka, scoring once and providing three assists, that former Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane said he can go on to be "one of the greatest players of all time".
"At this moment in time, he is an amazing footballer. The package, his running power, his delivery, his goal threat," Keane said.
Keane's praise was echoed by Bournemouth's Alex Scott, who made his first England start alongside Bellingham and Elliot Anderson in midfield against Croatia.
"Honestly, I've never seen anything like it," Scott said.
"He's even better in person, seeing it up close and being on the same pitch as him, he's the best midfielder in the world.
"On the pitch his ability is scary and that's the benchmark we need to live up to."
England winger Bukayo Saka added: "He was special, (I'm) happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team."
Tuchel said Kane's relationship with Bellingham has blossomed on and off the pitch in recent months, paving the way for the explosion of creativity and goals from the pair.
Fittingly, it was Bellingham who took the captain's armband from Kane when the striker was replaced late in the Croatia match.
"They get better and better. They love playing with each other. They understand each other better," Tuchel said.
"We adjusted our positioning a little bit after the World Cup. Jude almost plays a little bit more offensive for us. That's where I see him in the most dangerous position."

6d472a9e4aebc7a9: SEREMBAN, Oct 5 — The Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has once again reaffirmed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.

DKU secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin said Tuanku Muhriz was elected by the Undangs and proclaimed as the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar on Dec 29, 2008, before being officially installed in accordance with the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS) on Oct 26, 2009.
He said Tuanku Muhriz continued to hold the position, as well as serving as chairman of the DKU under Article 19.

“The UUTKNS 1959 provides that the only lawful way for the position to become vacant is if it is established that the Undangs have called upon His Royal Highness to abdicate or step down. Article 10 requires a proper and full enquiry by the Undangs; a determination that the grounds specified under Article 10 exist.
“The exercise of that power by persons lawfully holding the office of Undang in the number required under Article 29; and a proclamation under Article 10(2),” he said in a statement yesterday.
Raja Norazli said none of these requirements had been fulfilled.
He said Tuanku Muhriz had continued to discharge the functions of the Yang Dipertuan Besar since April 19, while the council continued to sit with His Royal Highness as its chairman.
As such, he said there was no vacancy in the office of Yang Dipertuan Besar.
“Article 11 only applies when the position is vacant, and could not be invoked to elect a successor as long as the office is lawfully occupied.

“The tenure of Tuanku Muhriz in the position can only be terminated in the manner provided for under the UUTKNS 1959. The council does not recognise any other person as holding the position,” he said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, secretary of the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), reads his special statement at his office in Seremban, October 4, 2026. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, Raja Norazli said Tuanku Muhriz did not intervene in Luak Sungei Ujong affairs during the April 17 sitting.
He said the records showed that the matter brought before the DKU was a complaint lodged by representatives of the Telaga Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong, namely Ibu Soko and Waris Klana Hulu.
“They dismissed Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak as Undang in accordance with the customs of the Luak, with the dismissal letter handed to him on May 13, 2025.

“He said Tuanku Muhriz had made it clear that, under Article 14(1) and (3), the customary authority to choose, appoint and dismiss an Undang rests with the Luak itself, and that no member of the Dewan, ‘including His Royal Highness himself’, has the power to support or oppose such a decision,” he said.
He said the DKU therefore recognised the dismissal as a decision by the Luak under its own customs under Article 14(3).

“The members were consulted before the conclusion was reached, and the minutes showed that no further objections were raised after Tuanku Muhriz, as Speaker of the Dewan, announced the Dewan’s decision to accept the dismissal,” he said.
He said neither the DKU nor Tuanku Muhriz had dismissed any Undang.
Raja Norazli explained that the Dewan accepted the Luak’s decision to dismiss the Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong.

“Therefore, the April 17 sitting was not an intervention in the affairs of the Luak. Rather, it was the Dewan carrying out its function under Article 16 to receive and advise on a decision already made by the Luak in accordance with its customs,” he said.
Raja Norazli also said the Luak had dismissed Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak as Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong under its customs, effective May 13, 2025 (advice dated April 17, 2026).
Maarof Mat Rashad, meanwhile, was dismissed as Undang of Luak Jelebu under the Luak’s customs, effective May 31, 2023 (advice dated July 31, 2026).

“Abdul Rahim Yasin was never formally appointed as Undang of Luak Rembau in accordance with the prescribed customs because his appointment was never completed through the Istiadat Menzahirkan Kejadian Undang ceremony (advice dated July 31),” he said.

Raja Norazli said Badarudin Abdul Khalid had ceased to hold the position of Dato’ Shahbandar Sungei Ujong following a Luruh Pusaka declaration by anak waris and Ibu Soko Waris di Ayer on July 30, 2026, which was affirmed on July 31, 2026.
“Therefore, the current Undang are Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari for Luak Sungei Ujong and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid for Luak Rembau.

“Datuk Johan Pahlawan Lela Perkasa Setiawan Datuk Muhammed Abdullah is the Undang of Luak Johol, while the positions of Undang of Luak Jelebu and Dato’ Shahbandar Sungei Ujong are currently vacant,” he said.

He said the DKU had therefore maintained its decision of July 31, 2026 that the document dated April 19, 2026 did not comply with Article 10, was unconstitutional and had no effect, and that no valid process had resulted in Tuanku Muhriz ceasing to hold the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Raja Norazli also said the DKU continued to recognise Tuanku Muhriz as Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and Speaker of the Dewan under Article 19, did not recognise any vacancy in either position, and did not recognise anyone else as holding them.

He said the DKU also called on all state and federal civil servants to continue administering the state in accordance with the law and the lawful chain of command, and required anyone claiming that a “sufficient and full investigation” had been conducted to present the complete record of the process before a forum with jurisdiction.
“All parties are also urged to respect court proceedings, maintain public order, and not invoke custom as a reason to disregard the UUTKNS 1959,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The initials UUTKNS stands for Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan, the Malay term for the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan.

1fbbc393988981c7: BACKA TOPOLA, Serbia: Israel's players wore black armbands in their Nations League draw against Ireland on Sunday to commemorate the victims of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack, after Irish players wore them to protest the war in Gaza.
The simple black armbands were inscribed with the numbers "7.10" to mark the date of the attack.

Just as in last week's first match in Hungary which Ireland won 3-0, the Irish players again bowed their heads during the Israeli anthem and the teams refused to shake hands before the 1-1 draw, this time played in the small Serbian town of Backa Topola.
The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had refused to host Israel on Irish soil for security reasons, following calls to boycott the matches.
The two matches against Israel have sparked controversy in Ireland, which has long supported the Palestinian cause.
"I'm absolutely delighted this has finished, it has taken a toll on all of us," said Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson.
"I've given so much credit to the players, they have been absolutely amazing in tough times and I wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks."
On Sunday, Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead from the penalty spot on 39 minutes after Dor Peretz fouled Jimmy Dunne.
The Real Betis striker has now scored 10 of the last 13 competitive goals for the Republic.
But Peretz stabbed in an equaliser two minutes after half-time, sending in from close range after a shot deflected off Ireland defender Liam Scales and into his path.
The tension of the match was evident when the two squads clashed as they left the pitch at half-time.
The result complicates Ireland's qualification task as they now lie third in Group 3 of League B behind Austria and Kosovo. Israel are bottom with two points.
"It felt like a friendly .. there were no people watching, no spark in the game," said Hallgrimsson.
"There was I think lesser emotions involved in this game and I think that was the difference.
"We should have done better in the first half and killed the game."
The Israeli Football Association said Sunday that the request to wear black armbands had been approved by European football's governing body UEFA.
The Hamas-led attack was the deadliest in Israeli history and killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

The massive Israeli offensive in response has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Ireland's 2-2 draw against Austria in Dublin on Thursday was twice briefly interrupted by demonstrations in support of the Palestinians.
Israel has been unable to host international matches on its own soil because of security risks since the outbreak of the war in Gaza.

The first match went ahead in Hungary instead, with Ireland beating Israel following a turbulent build-up in which the Irish squad voted to fulfil the fixture after goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pulled out a day before the game.

On Saturday, Ireland's press conference in Serbia was cut short as Hallgrimsson fielded questions from Israeli journalists, including one about an Omani pilot's attack on a flydubai flight heading for Tel Aviv earlier in the week.

The Icelander sparked a diplomatic row over the games last month by saying: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."
The Israeli association accused him of "stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy."
On Sunday, Hallgrimsson said in hindsight he would have done things differently.
"Today I would think I did a mistake there because my feelings and my opinion should be set aside when I'm spokesman for an organisation and a group," he said in Serbia.

579920e412f59bf7: BRASILIA: Brazilian senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the far-right former leader Jair Bolsonaro, finished ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's election, which will go to a run-off in three weeks.
In a surprise result that defied opinion poll projections showing Lula in the lead, Flavio Bolsonaro scored 47% of the vote to the incumbent's 45%.
If Bolsonaro triumphs in the Oct 25 election, Brazil will be the latest country to swing to the right in Latin America, a trend championed by US president Donald Trump.
The election results included a series of landslide wins for the right in parliament in a massive setback to Lula, who at almost 81 is seeking a fourth term in office to cement his legacy.
The veteran leftist branded the vote a battle between democracy and "barbarism," warning voters that Brazil's sovereignty was at stake in the face of US pressure.
Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, was little known nationally before his jailed father anointed him as his political heir, and he had never expressed ambition to follow in his footsteps.
However, his father's powerful name won over the country's conservative base and he slid past Lula despite a campaign marked by scandals and mudslinging.
Voters in the deeply polarized nation were left jaded by familiar choices, and few voted with conviction.

Oscarina de Oliveira, a 62-year-old caregiver, told AFP she had planned to vote for Lula, as she always has. But "when I got there, I switched to Bolsonaro. Just to see what happens, to see if anything changes."
Bolsonaro dynasty
It emerged during the campaign that Flavio Bolsonaro was under investigation for corruption over the financing of the biopic "Dark Horse" about his father.
The move was bankrolled by jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, who is under investigation for a massive financial scandal.
For many voters, this did little to move the needle.

"Things are truly terrible. As far as I'm concerned, the left just doesn't work anymore," said tech worker Joao Batista, 36, in the Rocinha favela, saying he was fed up with the "horrible" expense of basic goods.
The Vorcaro probe also led to a rare public clash on the Supreme Court which fuelled distrust in institutions and was seen by experts as damaging to Lula's campaign.

The elections proved a triumphant comeback for the Bolsonaro family after Jair Bolsonaro lost a re-election bid in 2022, leading to violent riots in the capital and his conviction last year for attempting a coup.
Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro and another one of Jair Bolsonaro's sons, Carlos Bolsonaro, both secured seats in the senate.
Jair Bolsonaro's youngest son Jair Renan, 28, was elected as a federal lawmaker.
Trump watching
Trump had said he was watching the election "very closely," but did not endorse Flavio Bolsonaro.
The US president has wielded tariffs and sanctions to pressure Brasilia over complaints ranging from the trial against his ally Jair Bolsonaro to alleged unfair trade practices.
Lula repeatedly warned him not to "meddle" in the elections.
He also vowed Brazil would retain control over the development of its vast reserves of rare earths, which have attracted interest from Washington and other foreign powers.
"I support Lula because he stands up for the poor. Flavio will sell our Brazil off to foreigners," said Victor Jorge Martins, a 25-year-old event planner.
Flavio Bolsonaro has pitched Brazil as a "solution" to ease US dependence on China for these critical minerals.
Climate change absent

Revered for social welfare programmes that lifted millions out of poverty, Lula made a dramatic comeback to office in the 2022 elections after being jailed on a corruption conviction that was later thrown out on procedural grounds.
In his third term he oversaw a drop in inflation and unemployment, but voters complain about a high cost of living.
Lula has also sharply curbed deforestation in the Amazon, while backing oil exploration.
Despite a growing number of extreme weather events in Brazil, climate change has been absent from the campaign.
"It is important to elect a candidate who defends our territory, who defends nature," said Tainara da Costa Cruz, 22, who lives along the banks of the Rio Negro in Amazonas state and voted for Lula.
5f53ea4d51298cd9: TOKYO: Japan no longer needs expansionary fiscal and monetary policies aimed at boosting demand, former Bank of Japan (BOJ) board member Asahi Noguchi told Reuters, projecting another interest rate hike by the central bank in December.

The remarks by Noguchi, a reflationist academic who served at the BOJ until March, highlight how years of rising inflation and wages are causing a shift in mindset among those who were once advocates of big spending and loose monetary policy.

"Underlying inflation is near the BOJ's 2.0 per cent target and wages are becoming embedded at levels consistent with 2.0 per cent inflation. If so, it would be too risky to implement policies that boost demand," Noguchi said in an interview on Friday.

After spending years treading cautiously in policy normalisation, the BOJ picked up pace in raising rates by hiking in June and September as the Iran war-induced energy shock added to price pressures from rising import costs via a weak yen.
While the BOJ probably hoped to keep moving cautiously to prevent another economic downturn, it had little choice but to speed up rate hikes to avoid causing unwelcome yen falls, Noguchi said.
"It's hard for the BOJ alone to move slowly when other central banks are shifting to a rate-hike mode amid global inflationary pressures," he said.
"The BOJ won't openly say so but it's mostly concerned about the risk of a yen slide below 160 versus the dollar that would cause a fresh wave of food inflation."

A weak yen has become a headache for Japan as it boosts import costs. The yen has hovered around 158, near the 160 line seen by markets, heightening the chance of yen intervention, as prospects of near-term US rate hikes strengthen the dollar.

While receding prospects of a US rate hike in October will likely allow the BOJ to sit pat this month, there is a good chance it will raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent from the current 1.25 per cent in December, Noguchi said.

The BOJ could eventually lift its policy rate to 1.75 per cent or even 2.0 per cent, depending on how far its US counterpart could raise rates and on developments in the Middle East conflict, he said.
While a rate hike to 1.75 per cent is unlikely to hurt the economy, an increase to 2.0 per cent could be risky, as it could shock households and firms long used to ultra-low borrowing costs, he said.
"With so much uncertainty on how its rate hikes affect the economy, the BOJ probably wants to take things very slowly," Noguchi said. "But market forces won't let it do so."

Noguchi joined the BOJ board in 2021 as a reflationist advocate of aggressive monetary easing. He dissented to the BOJ's decision to end negative rates in 2024 and a hike to 0.25 per cent that year. But he voted for two rate rises thereafter.

Investors have sold yen and Japanese government bonds on concern the BOJ may be behind the curve on inflation. Premier Sanae Takaichi's big spending plans are also blamed for the selloff by heightening attention to Japan's worsening finances.

With the output gap now positive, Japan must avoid ramping up spending, as excessively loose fiscal policy could push up bond yields and dampen corporate investment, said Noguchi, who is currently a professor at Japan's Senshu University.

"Japan doesn't need policies to boost demand, as expansionary fiscal policy would crowd out private investment, while too-low interest rates would cause yen falls," Noguchi said. "In short, reflationary policies no longer have a role to play in Japan."
68b79907135bfa72: PETALING JAYA: The 2027 federal budget should highlight equitable access to education, advanced talent development, and turning research into action, says the chairman of a research and policy institute.
Shahir Liew, who heads the advisory council of the Asian Institute for Policy and Engagement, said access to education remains important to students from underserved and lower-income backgrounds.

The national budget, therefore, must continue to ensure Malaysians are not denied educational opportunities because of financial barriers, he said. The government should also roll out initiatives to encourage graduates to take on research-specific roles, and also postgraduate pathways to help meet its goal of 200 researchers, scientists, engineers and technologists (RSET) per 10,000 members of the workforce.

Citing data from the higher education ministry, Shahir said that as of December 2025, postgraduate enrolment stood at approximately 114,600 students, representing about 9% of higher-education enrolment.

“One important but underutilised source of future RSET talent is the large pool of experienced engineers, scientists, technologists and professionals already working in Malaysian industry,” he told FMT.
According to the Malaysian Science and Technology Information Centre (Mastic), the country had approximately 55 researchers per 10,000 workforce in 2023.

“Flexible, part-time and industry-embedded postgraduate research pathways can help convert existing expertise into research and innovation capability," Shahir said. He urged the government to set aside funds to strengthen the pathway between universities, industry, government and society.

Shahir said Mastic data show that businesses direct the majority of their R&D spending toward experimental development, while universities remain focused on basic and applied research. More co-funded, industry-linked projects can help bridge this gap and accelerate commercialisation, he said.

Shahir, who is also the vice provost of research and knowledge exchange of University of Nottingham Malaysia, said existing tax incentives that encourage company investment in talent development could be expanded to include employer-sponsored postgraduate research.
5c2b0d11baac1e99: PETALING JAYA: Belanjawan Persekutuan 2027 harus menekankan akses saksama kepada pendidikan, pembangunan bakat berkemahiran tinggi dan usaha menterjemahkan penyelidikan kepada tindakan, kata pengerusi sebuah institut penyelidikan dan dasar.

Shahir Liew, yang mengetuai majlis penasihat Asian Institute for Policy and Engagement, berkata akses kepada pendidikan kekal penting bagi pelajar yang ketinggalan dan dengan latar belakang keluarga berpendapatan rendah.
Oleh itu, katanya, belanjawan negara mesti terus memastikan rakyat Malaysia tidak dinafikan peluang pendidikan disebabkan kekangan kewangan.

Kerajaan juga harus melaksanakan inisiatif untuk menggalakkan graduan mengambil peranan khusus dalam penyelidikan, serta laluan pengajian pascasiswazah bagi membantu mencapai matlamatnya untuk mempunyai 200 penyelidik, saintis, jurutera dan teknologis (RSET) bagi setiap 10,000 tenaga kerja.

Memetik data Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi, Shahir berkata setakat Disember 2025, jumlah pendaftaran pascasiswazah kira-kira 114,600 pelajar, mewakili kira-kira 9% daripada jumlah pendaftaran pendidikan tinggi.

“Salah satu sumber bakat RSET masa depan yang penting tetapi kurang dimanfaatkan ialah kumpulan besar jurutera, saintis, teknologis dan golongan profesional berpengalaman yang sudah bekerja dalam industri Malaysia,” katanya kepada FMT.
Menurut Pusat Maklumat Sains dan Teknologi Malaysia, negara mempunyai kira-kira 55 penyelidik bagi setiap 10,000 tenaga kerja pada 2023.
“Laluan penyelidikan pascasiswazah yang fleksibel, separuh masa dan berasaskan industri boleh membantu mengubah kepakaran sedia ada kepada keupayaan penyelidikan dan inovasi,” kata Shahir.
Beliau menggesa kerajaan memperuntukkan dana untuk memperkukuh laluan antara universiti, industri, kerajaan dan masyarakat.

Shahir berkata data Mastic menunjukkan perniagaan menyalurkan sebahagian besar perbelanjaan penyelidikan dan pembangunan (R&D) mereka kepada pembangunan eksperimen, manakala universiti kekal memberi tumpuan kepada penyelidikan asas dan gunaan.
Lebih banyak projek yang dibiayai bersama dan berkaitan dengan industri boleh membantu merapatkan jurang ini serta mempercepat pengkomersialan, katanya.

Shahir, yang juga naib provos penyelidikan dan pertukaran pengetahuan Universiti Nottingham Malaysia, berkata insentif cukai sedia ada yang menggalakkan pelaburan syarikat dalam pembangunan bakat boleh diperluaskan untuk merangkumi penyelidikan pascasiswazah yang ditaja oleh majikan.
4b3cbfbc5f5a9ce8: PETALING JAYA: When skin suddenly begins to sting, itch or turn red, it can be tempting to add more products in the hope that one of them will bring relief.

Yet doing so can make it harder to identify what caused the reaction. For sensitive or irritated skin, a scaled-back routine comprising a gentle cleanser, moisturiser and sunscreen may be a better place to start.
Still, “natural”, “hypoallergenic” and “additive-free” are not guarantees that a product will suit everyone. What matters is the formulation as a whole and how an individual’s skin responds to it.
Here are five commonly discussed ingredients and what sensitive-skin users should know about them.
1. Fragrance
Fragrance is among the better-known triggers of cosmetic allergies. Reactions can include itching, redness and swelling, sometimes appearing hours or even days after exposure.
Both synthetic scents and naturally derived fragrance ingredients, including some essential oils and botanical extracts, can cause reactions. “Natural” does not necessarily mean non-irritating.

The American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) recommends looking for products labelled “fragrance-free” rather than merely “unscented”, as the latter may still contain ingredients intended to mask other smells.
2. Certain types of alcohol

Not every ingredient containing the word “alcohol” has the same effect on skin. Short-chain alcohols such as ethanol and denatured alcohol are often used to help products feel lighter or dry more quickly.
Depending on their concentration and the overall formulation, however, they may sting or feel drying on already-irritated skin.
A 2025 laboratory study found that a cream containing ethanol increased water loss and reduced hydration in intact skin samples, although its effects differed in skin that was already irritated.
These should not be confused with fatty alcohols such as cetyl, stearyl and cetearyl alcohol, which are generally used as emollients or to improve a product’s texture.
3. Colour additives
Colour is often added to make skincare products more visually appealing, but it does not necessarily offer any benefit to the skin.

The US Food and Drug Administration includes dyes among several classes of cosmetic ingredients that can cause allergic reactions in some people. However, this does not mean every colour additive is harmful or that synthetic dyes automatically clog pores.

Those with a history of reactions may prefer colour-free formulas, particularly while trying to identify a trigger. Checking the full ingredient list is more useful than judging a product by its appearance alone.
4. Lanolin
Derived from wool, lanolin is used in rich creams and ointments as it helps soften skin and reduce moisture loss.

It can, however, cause allergic contact dermatitis in some individuals, particularly those who already have damaged or inflamed skin. This makes it worth avoiding if a person has previously reacted to it or received a positive result during medical patch testing.
Still, lanolin is not universally irritating. Many people can use it without difficulty, so its presence alone does not make a product unsuitable for sensitive skin.
5. Mineral oil
Despite its petroleum origins, cosmetic-grade mineral oil is not inherently harmful. It is an occlusive ingredient, meaning it forms a layer over the skin that slows moisture loss.
Mineral oil has long been used in moisturisers for dry skin, and a randomised clinical trial found it effective in treating mild to moderate dryness.

Heavier or highly occlusive products may aggravate acne or folliculitis in certain users, but individual response and the overall formulation matter. As such, mineral oil should not automatically be blamed for every breakout.
How should you approach a new skincare product?
Rather than changing an entire routine at once, introduce a product at a time. This makes it easier to identify the culprit if a reaction develops.
The AAD recommends applying a new product to a small test area twice daily for seven to 10 days before using it more widely.
Stop using it if the skin becomes red, itchy or swollen. Persistent or recurring reactions should be assessed by a dermatologist, who may recommend medical patch testing to identify an allergy.

Ultimately, caring for sensitive skin is not about declaring long lists of ingredients “good” or “bad”. Sometimes less really is more - but the goal is a simple, well-tolerated routine, not fear of everything on the label.

e02ee40636b118e5: NEW YORK: A shooting early on Sunday at a Georgia block party left two people dead and almost three dozen injured, some critically, local and state officials said.
Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavy told a news conference that two men, aged 21 and 23, were shot dead in Vienna, Georgia, about 135 miles (216 km) south of Atlanta.
Thirty-five people were injured, mostly by gunshot wounds, officials told reporters.
They said hundreds of people had attended the event, which came at the end of Dooly County High School's homecoming week.
Authorities do not believe there is a remaining threat to the public, but have not publicly named any suspects or persons of interest, and have not identified a motive for the shooting.
"We don't want to presume as to what caused it," said Chris Hosey, director of the Georgia Bureau of Investigation.
Those wounded range in age from 14 to 51, officials said. — REUTERS
efea7cdc63844ff8: KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji's (TH) investment strategy and risk management will be among the issues raised when the Dewan Rakyat resumes sitting today.

Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) is scheduled to ask the Prime Minister about measures to diversify TH's investment portfolio and ensure the sustainability of its funds, according to the parliament's order paper.
He will also ask about measures being taken to ensure TH can continue helping Malaysians meet the cost of performing the haj.

The safety of Malaysians abroad will also come under scrutiny, with Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) scheduled to ask the foreign minister about measures to strengthen the registration system for Malaysians travelling or staying abroad.
He will also ask whether registration should be made compulsory for high-risk destinations to ensure Malaysians can be located and assisted promptly in the event of a tragedy, disaster or emergency.

Food security and dependence on imports will also be raised, with Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) scheduled to ask the agriculture and food security minister about efforts to reduce food imports, which exceeded RM90 billion in 2025, as well as action against the dumping of imported products.

Meanwhile, Oscar Ling Chai Yew (PH-Sibu) will ask the higher education minister about the latest status of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) following its repeal, including the implementation timeline, transition mechanism and status of drafting the new legislation.

The latest developments in negotiations between the federal and Sarawak governments on the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) relating to regulatory powers over oil and gas, will be raised by Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo).

Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa (PH-Sekijang) is scheduled to ask the economy minister about the timeline for tabling the National Ageing Action Plan in the Dewan Rakyat and the setting of specific indicators to measure the silver economy's contribution to gross domestic product (GDP).

Datuk Dr Ku Abd Rahman Ku Ismail (PN-Kubang Pasu) will also ask the digital minister about the government's position on calls to slow down artificial intelligence (AI) development and the proposed drafting of the Malaysian AI Act.
The sitting will also see the first readings of two Bills — the Sports Development (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the youth and sports minister and the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the health minister.

It will also continue with briefings on three reports by Parliamentary Select Committees and the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), including those on refugee management in Malaysia and the management of court bail payments through the e-Jamin system.
The third meeting of the fifth session of the 15th Parliament will run for 37 days until Dec 8.
